item.content:encoded:
RedSoxRoundtable's Zach Coe discusses starter Sonny Gray joining Red Sox Hall of Famer Tim Wakefield in franchise history. Be sure to join our FREE community over on RedSoxRoundtable.com!
The Boston Red Sox avoided a sweep at the hands of the Texas Rangers on Thursday night thanks to a 4-3 win that was powered by an eighth-inning, go-ahead, three-run home run off the bat of shortstop Trevor Story. While Story's big swing was undoubtedly the story of the game, Boston was in position to win because of Sonny Gray's fantastic start, a start that saw him join Red Sox Hall of Famer Tim Wakefield in the history books.
Gray tossed 6.1 innings, allowing just three earned runs on three hits while striking out six and walking three. According to Red Sox Nation Stats on Twitter/X, Gray became the first pitcher aged 36 or older to log 21 or more starts of six or more innings pitched since Wakefield did so in 2008.
Gray has been nothing short of a revelation since arriving in Boston on an offseason deal with the St. Louis Cardinals. The 36-year-old veteran was brought in, in part, to be the "Robin" to Garrett Crochet's "Batman." However, because of the shoulder injury that has kept Crochet out of the rotation since late April, Gray has served as "Batman" just as well as the 2025 American League Cy Young Award runner-up could have.
In Crochet's absence, Gray has posted a 2.57 ERA in 23 starts, spanning 140 innings pitched. The team has gone 17-6 in those starts. Not only has Gray been Boston's best starter since the Crochet injury, but he's also been one of the best arms in baseball in the stretch, with his ERA ranking as the sixth-lowest mark over that time.
Overall, Gray has posted a 2.82 ERA that ranks fifth best among all American League starters, doing it in 163 innings with an fWAR of 3.2 that sits just outside the top 10 at No. 11. Perhaps most importantly, even when the 36-year-old veteran doesn't have his best stuff, he keeps the team in a position to win, as was evident on Thursday night.
When Gray was first acquired, many questioned whether he could still be a top of the rotation arm. Now, after answering those questions with a season that'll likely see him finish top five in American League Cy Young Award voting, the only question that remains is whether he'll return for 2027 and beyond.
Up next for the Sox
After dropping two of three in Texas, the Red Sox' final regular-season road trip rolls on as they open a three-game series at Tropicana Field against the likely American League East champion Tampa Bay Rays on Friday night. Ranger Suarez (7-4, 3.33 ERA) gets the start for Boston opposite Ian Seymour (9-6, 4.27 ERA) for Tampa Bay. First pitch is set for 7:10 p.m. ET.

item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox are beginning a major weekend series Friday night when they travel to Tampa Bay to take on the American League-leading Rays.
While the series isn't likely going to feature center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela for the Red Sox as he continues to rehab a right quad injury, the team still announced some notable personal news about the first-time All-Star.
It's Rafaela's 26th Birthday!
While it'd be nice to see Rafaela return to action, it is in fact his 26th birthday on Friday, which the Red Sox acknowledged with a post on social media.
"Ceddy's day!" the Red Sox posted on X.
Red Sox Fans React on Social Media
The Boston fanbase has embraced Rafaela since he made his debut with the organization in 2023, and his play in the outfield and at the plate has made him a fan favorite.
On Friday, they made sure to wish Rafaela a happy birthday.
"Happy birthday to the platinum glover of the American League," a fan said.
Someone else added, "Need you back in that lineup King!"
Another person wrote, "happy birthday king."
"HAPPY BIRTHDAY TO HIM!" a fan shared.
One more commented, "I LOVE HIMMMMMM HAPPY BIRTHDAY CEDDANNEEE."
Looking at Rafaela's 2026 Season
Rafaela has appeared in 135 games for Boston this season, and across 535 at-bats, he's recorded 67 runs, 151 hits, 16 home runs, and 70 RBIs while hitting .282 with a .443 slugging percentage and a .760 OPS.
He's a crucial piece to the puzzle for the Red Sox to accomplish what they envision in an American League that seems pretty wide open outside of their two division opponents, the Rays and the New York Yankees.
Boston is obviously more than familiar with both teams, and if it came to a series setting, they'd likely be very confident they can be competitive and hold their own.
The latest update on Rafaela's injury is that he's likely targeting a return during the final homestand next week, but he hasn't had any notable setbacks.

As it turns out, he is. After c
item.content:encoded:
When the Boston Red Sox lost shortstop Trevor Story to an injury earlier this year, one big question was how they were going to replace him. Interim manager Chad Tracy used a couple of different players who more than held things down until the veteran was going to return.
When Story was eligible to return, Andruw Monasterio found himself as the odd man out at shortstop. However, Story had to prove that he was healthy enough to hold down the job late in the season.
As it turns out, he is. After coming up clutch on Thursday night, Story didn't mince words about the noise that there is outside the locker room about him.
Boston Red Sox Shortstop Trevor Story Drops Honest Quote on Outside Noise
Trailing 3-0 against the Texas Rangers on Thursday night in Arlington, Boston was staring at being swept as the game moved into the late innings. After they plated a run in the top of the seventh on a Roman Anthony fielder's choice.
In the top of the eighth, Story stepped up to the plate with two runners on and one out. Story crushed a curveball from Texas' Jacob Latz for a three-run home run and 4-3 lead. The Red Sox got the final six outs to secure a one-run win. After the game, Story didn't mince words about the outside noise and hearing it.
"I'm not really motivated by outside noise, but you hear it," said Story, per Alex Speier of the Boston Globe. "I try to use it in the way that fits me best. The point of getting the surgery was to come back and try to be the player that I know I can be, and it's starting to show."
Halfway through the month of September, Story is slashing .327/.339/.473 in September with one home run and six RBIs.
"He's been great," Tracy said, per Perla Paredes of MLB.com. "He's got a hit in every game but one. That was a hell of an at-bat against a really good pitcher in a really big spot and a huge swing. Obviously needed a win, but all the credit to him.
"You're one pitch away in a spot like that, where he can change a game, like we saw it numerous times in the second half of last year. So, like I said, it was a massive swing."
Trevor Story Looking To Find Swing Before Playoffs
There are nine games for the Red Sox before the playoffs begin. Boston is likely headed for an American League wild-card series against the New York Yankees. The series for the second straight year will be in the Bronx.
Boston has a three-game series against the first-place Tampa Bay Rays this weekend in Central Florida. They then close out the season with a pair of three-game series at home against the Cleveland Guardians and Chicago Cubs.
Finishing the regular season strong will be key. Boston has struggled in September and is limping into the playoffs. A healthy Story could be key for Boston come postseason baseball.

item.content:encoded:
The Wild Card isn't the only race the Chicago Cubs are winning.
With an off-day on Thursday, the Cubs flew down to Louisville, Kentucky, to support one of their marquee players. Alex Bregman's horse, Act of Parliament, took the track at the famous Churchill Downs, and the rest is history!
Led by jockey Axel Concepcion, Bregman's horse came away victorious. And it's safe to say his Cubs teammates were thrilled to be in attendance.
Numerous posts on social media show the Cubs going absolutely bonkers for Bregman. An enormous huddle formed in the winner's circle, where Concepcion was tossed sky-high. Speaking of which, high fives were aplenty!
Even the typically stoic Craig Counsell couldn't help but jump around like a kid.
Craig Counsell in the middle of it going nuts https://t.co/QLyTogEG1u
- Brett Taylor (@Brett_A_Taylor) September 18, 2026
To make matters more fun, it appears as if several were dressed for the occasion. This included some Debry-inspired garb, but some players went as far as sporting their own jockey outfits.
Ryan Rolison decided to take a step further, though, channeling his inner horse.
Alex Bregman also shared a video on Instagram of Pete Crow-Armstrong meeting with his horse before the race. As the Cubs' likely NL MVP can be seen petting Act of Parliament, Bregman included a caption that read, "PCA pep talk we couldn't lose."
Bregman might want to consider bringing Crow-Armstrong to all his races from now on. Have you seen the last few months?
Alex Bregman's Instagram story shows the Cubs dressed up for a night at the racetrack on their flight and Pete Crow-Armstrong petting one of the ponies and giving it a "pep talk" pic.twitter.com/OOsnrmmwnN
- Josh Frydman (@Josh_Frydman) September 18, 2026
A Cubs Bonding Moment Before the Stretch Run
As silly as it may sound, a moment like that could prove to be a lot more than just a fun memory for this Chicago Cubs team.
Team morale has likely been rocked in recent weeks as they officially lost their footing in the NL Central race. Even more troubling, the Cubs have watched their sizeable Wild Card lead shrink thanks to a late-season surge from the Philadelphia Phillies. While they maintain the No. 1 spot at this point in time, they only have their regular-season tiebreaker to thank for that. Both teams are neck-and-neck with an 85-68 record on the season.
This means the Cubs' final nine games of the 2026 campaign are going to hold tremendous weight. You never quite know how a team will respond to that kind of pressure, but who's to say Thursday's party at Churchill Downs can't serve as the momentum boost they need!
Bregman's horse walking away victorious also feels poetic. The veteran struggled for much of the season, only to catch his rhythm at the perfect time. He's now looked like exactly the star the Cubs thought they were signing to a five-year deal this offseason. Over his last month of action, Bregman has slashed .313/.394/.670. In his last seven games alone, he has nine hits, two homers, and six RBIs.
Everything is coming up Bregman, and the Cubs sure hope that continues over the next several weeks!

item.title: [Just Baseball] Is Mickey Gasper More Than a Flash in the Pan for the Red Sox? | Just Baseball
item.dc:creator: Gabe Shumway

item.content:encoded:
For 13 games in 2024, Mickey Gasper came up to the plate for the Boston Red Sox. In many cases, the NESN cameras cut to his eager parents as they awaited his first MLB hit.
A hit that never came. In 2024, at least.
Gasper’s journey to the big leagues was unconventional. He played at Bryant University, an NEC school whose only athletic national championship victory came from its athletic band and cheer team.
At the time, Bryant was a baseball team at the top of its conference. Gasper became a major part of this sustained success, as he dominated in his sophomore, junior, and senior seasons, both with Bryant and in summer leagues. This included the Cape Cod Baseball League, the most competitive summer baseball circuit in the country.
But this success never fully translated to his first few seasons in pro ball.
Gasper was drafted by the Yankees in the 27th round of the 2018 MLB Draft. This round doesn’t even exist in 2026. Without the pedigree of a top-round talent, Gasper did not receive the benefit of the doubt for his skills in the minor leagues. Instead, he bounced around, climbed slowly, and eventually, after a 2024 hot streak, got the call-up to Boston at 28 years old.
2024: no hits in Boston. 2025: a .488 OPS in Minnesota. It looked as if the sun may have finally set on Gasper’s chance to be a big league mainstay.
Then came one of the crazier “Linsanity”-adjacent runs Red Sox fans have seen. But with the hot streak still burning fingers, the baseball world is pondering… is this a two-month heater or a sign of things to come?
Let’s dive into the numbers behind Gasper’s career-defining stretch at age 30.
Stats updated prior to games on September 17.
What Do the Underlying Numbers Say?
Gasper’s underlying numbers say two very different things. On one hand, his .373 OBP is backed up by a patient approach and strong understanding of the strike zone. His power, however, is reflected highly in his expected stats, while his bat speed and exit velocities show signs of regression.
In many ways, Gasper’s lack of elite athleticism or power on the surface makes his hot streak all the more impressive. He doesn’t have quick enough hands to generate major power or hit to all fields at an elite level. Instead, he chooses his battles remarkably well.
This mix of extreme patience, including a 15.0% strikeout rate and 12.6% walk rate, allows Gasper to maintain an All-Star-caliber xSLG and xwOBA. His exit velocity and hard-hit rate are average at best, but because he is so patient, Gasper picks his spots well. This means that he’s one of the league’s best in squared-up percentage.
This squared-up percentage could be a number that regresses over time, but Gasper’s breakout is supported in part by the underlying numbers. You can teach plate discipline, but it’s very hard to do this without compromising a hitter’s typical approach at the plate. Thankfully for Gasper, his plate discipline is a skill that gives him a higher floor at the MLB level.
In essence, Gasper is a player with a high floor and occasional bursts of a high ceiling. In many ways, he derives his value in similar ways to streaky, defense-first center fielders. He should generate value with the skills he is good at and occasionally go on hot streaks strong enough to carry a team on his back for a short period of time.
The one problem with this high ceiling is that Gasper is a positionless player. He played much of his career as a catcher, and Boston still has Gasper catch the occasional game. He has also played second base and left field in his MLB career, but these are not positions where fans can feel overly comfortable with him defensively.
If Gasper excels defensively at first or second base, there is certainly a chance he could become a mainstay. However, if he continues to produce fielding run values in the negatives, then he could lose opportunities to earn contracts or stay on MLB rosters as a reserve.
Comparing “Linsanity”-adjacent MLB Streaks
Basketball fans remember the magical season of Jeremy Lin, the Harvard graduate who got his shot with the Knicks due to injury and went on an all-time short-term run. Shortly after, he disappeared from the NBA world with an incredible legacy.
Gasper could go a few different directions in his career. Either he becomes a mainstay in the center of a lineup, a role player for years to come, or a minor league bat who bounces around other leagues as he ages.
Here are two similar runs where a player’s MLB tenure was dominant, but not long-lasting.
Yermin Mercedes
When the average American hears the word “Mercedes,” they probably think of the luxury car brand. When baseball diehards hear the word, they think of Yermin.
After April of 2024, the White Sox designated hitter/catcher was hitting over .400 with an OPS over 1.000 and five home runs. By June, Mercedes’ performance had slipped so mightily that he was sent back to the minor leagues.
After an underwhelming comeback attempt with San Francisco in 2022, Mercedes jumped around to select minor league teams. He last played in the Dominican and Mexican Winter Leagues in their 2024-25 seasons. He produced an OPS below .600 with both teams.
Aristides Aquino
It’s long been said that the best hitters are the ones who punish pitchers the most for each mistake they make on the mound. So when a 25-year-old, 6-foot-4, 220-pound outfielder out of the Dominican Republic was nicknamed “The Punisher,” he turned a lot of heads.
This is Aristides Aquino. At the time, there was a genuine belief that Aquino would turn the Cincinnati Reds around after a rough few seasons. They became the quintessential “underrated” pick entering 2020, so much so that they were not underrated at all.
And while the Reds did make the postseason in 2020, this was thanks to the expanded playoffs more than Aquino.
In 2019, Aquino hit for an .891 OPS across 56 games. The major difference, however, between Aquino and Gasper lies in the underlying metrics. Aquino struggled with plate discipline, whiffed at a high rate, and held expected stats that were far lower than his actual metrics. His slugging percentage, for example, was .576 in 2019 compared to an xSLG of .503.
His numbers in 2020 dipped and never quite recovered. In Aquino’s final season in 2022, he struggled at the plate again, but still produced a 1.3 rWAR thanks in large part to his impressive speed and 99th percentile arm strength.
Is Age Truly Just a Number?
Gasper is 30 years old. If the Red Sox make the ALCS, then Gasper will turn 31 at the start of that series. Mercedes was 28 during his “Linsanity” run, while Aquino was 25.
Obviously, this late start will eliminate certain achievements that Gasper can no longer pursue. But this isn’t just a lucky start for Gasper. He’s filled with highly sustainable underlying metrics that show his potential as an on-base threat for years to come.

item.content:encoded:
ARLINGTON, Texas — Trevor Story, who is from Irving, hit a go-ahead, three-run home run off Jacob Latz in the eighth inning Thursday night. The Boston Red Sox beat the Texas Rangers, 4-3, at Globe Life Field and kept Texas from a three-game sweep.
The Colorado Rockies drafted Story 45th overall in 2011 out of Irving High School, where he hit .488 as a senior. He had committed to LSU.
Boston trailed 3-1 entering the eighth. Story reached down for Latz’s second straight low curveball, an 80.3 mph pitch, and lined it over the wall in left-center field. It was his fourth home run of the season and his first since May 13. The loss dropped Texas one game behind the Houston Astros in the AL West.
The challenges of the year were part of it for Story.
“It meant a lot,” Story said. “Just the challenges of the year and all that, but just trying to be present in the moment to help the team win. And today was a good one, that was fun.”
Trevor Story Has A Hit in 15 Of 16 Games Since Sports Hernia Surgery
Boston placed Story on the 10-day injured list May 16 with a sports hernia that had bothered him since the spring. He had surgery later that month and was transferred to the 60-day IL on June 4. Since returning Aug. 30, Story has a hit in all but one of his 16 games, and he is riding an eight-game hitting streak. He is slashing .327/.339/.473 in September.
Story tries to use the outside noise in a way that fits him.
“It’s tough because I’m not really motivated by outside noise or anything,” Story explained. “But you hear it, and I try to use it in a way that fits me best. Like we said, that was the point of getting the surgery, to come back and try to be the player that I know I can be, and I’m starting to show that.”
Chad Tracy Says Trevor Story Delivered ‘A Massive Swing’
Jakob Junis set up the at-bat by walking Wilyer Abreu and hitting Willson Contreras to open the eighth. Latz then struck out Adley Rutschman. Story had just missed Latz’s fastball a couple of times earlier in the at-bat.
“I was looking for something just to put in play,” Story said. “[Latz has] a good fastball and just missed it a couple times, and I felt good about that. Just trying to get something in the zone and get on top of it, and was able to drive one out.”
Red Sox interim manager Chad Tracy said he saw Story change games that way numerous times in the second half of last season.
“He’s been great,” Tracy said. “He’s got a hit in every game but one. That was a hell of an at-bat against a really good pitcher in a really big spot and a huge swing. Obviously needed a win, but all the credit to him.”
“You’re one pitch away in a spot like that, where he can change a game, like we saw it numerous times in the second half of last year,” Tracy continued. “So, like I said, it was a massive swing.”
Boston (83-70) holds the second AL Wild Card spot, five games ahead of the Cleveland Guardians. The Red Sox open a three-game series against the Tampa Bay Rays on Friday and could clinch a postseason berth there.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Red Sox Monitoring Injury For Aroldis Chapman As Postseason Nears
item.dc:creator: Aaliyan Mohammed
item.description: Aroldis Chapman has not pitched since Sunday, and when he was not used with a one-run lead in the ninth inning on Thursday, interim manager Chad Tracy was asked for an explanation. Tracy said that Chapman was dealing with lat tightness. With the regular season winding down, that is not something that any Boston Red Sox fan wants to hear. item.content:encoded:
Aroldis Chapman has not pitched since Sunday, and when he was not used with a one-run lead in the ninth inning on Thursday, interim manager Chad Tracy was asked for an explanation.
Tracy said that Chapman was dealing with lat tightness. With the regular season winding down, that is not something that any Boston Red Sox fan wants to hear.
"We're going to be conservative with (it)," Tracy said postgame, per MLB.com's Perla Paredes. "It's getting better, but we're going to make sure it gets there. That's why he wasn't available tonight."
The good news is that Tracy said it's getting better. The Red Sox have Garrett Whitlock, who is more than capable of closing games, and some more bullpen reinforcements potentially on the way. However, Chapman has been one of the most dominant closers in baseball throughout his career, especially in Boston.
Chapman was the American League Reliever of the Year last year, posting a 1.17 ERA in 67 games. This year, he has a 1.95 ERA in 52 games and has 34 saves. The Red Sox's duo of him and Whitlock figures to be very important in October, but the 38-year-old needs to be healthy for that.
"Obviously, you guys know how diligent he is about his prep and getting in and getting treatment. So we'll just monitor it day to day," Tracy said.

item.content:encoded:
Only one minor league affiliate is still playing, and they were shut out on a two-hitter last night. But the show must go on!
Durham Bulls 2, Worcester Red Sox 0 (BOX)
Johan Oviedo beat the buzzer and got back on the mound in a rehab game on Thursday night. It was his first appearance at any level since March 30th (for Boston). Oviedo averaged 95.9 mph on both of his fastballs, and maxed out at 98.5 mph. He struck out four batters over 2 1/3 innings, allowing two hits, a walk, and one earned run, and was charged with the loss. While it might be aggressive to add him to the postseason roster, at least in round one, Oviedo was expected to be a key piece of the Red Sox rotation in 2026, acquired for Jhostynxon Garcia last offseason.
John Holobetz followed and was excellent, striking out eight over 4 1/3 shutout innings. Tyler Samaniego allowed a run in the eighth, and Noah Song threw a shutout ninth.
The Red Sox were shut down by former Cardinals great Jake Woodford, mustering just a double from Allan Castro, a single from Tomas Nido, and one walk at the plate.
With three games to go against the Bulls (TB) before the season comes to a close, Worcester is 39-31 in the second-half standings, three games out of first place, with three teams ahead of them in the standings. However, since Rochester is in first place in the second half, and also won the International League first half, Worcester is not a complete long shot to make the playoffs. If you want to look at the tiebreaker procedures in Triple-A, go nuts.
Michael Sansone (2-6, 6.55) gets the ball this evening at 6:05 for the Woo Sox. The Bulls will counter with Jesse Scholtens (3-4, 4.15).
The Woo Sox then play on Saturday at 4:05 and Sunday at 1:05. Numerous promotions remain during the final homestand, including opportunities to bring your children to play catch on the field and run the bases throughout the weekend. Get out there before summer comes to a close.
With this likely being the final Minor Lines of the year for me (Dean has you this weekend), I want to thank all of the readers at Over The Monster. It's such a joy talking baseball with all of you. You can follow me on Twitter @BobOsgood15, and you can reach me at redseatpodcast@gmail.com throughout the postseason and offseason.

item.content:encoded:
Red Sox Video
Boston Red Sox Affiliate Recap (September 17)
Triple-A Worcester Red Sox
Season Record: 75-66
Despite Worcester’s offense having no life, the pitching staff looked great in their 2-0 loss to the Durham Bulls (Tampa Bay Rays).
The WooSox tallied just two hits, not a recipe for success. Allan Castro cracked a two-out double in the first, and Tomás Nido hammered a one-out single in the ninth, but Worcester could not string together any more hits to bring them in.
Pitching just one game for Boston back in March, Johan Oviedo made his first rehab appearance since suffering a right elbow strain. Johan was the centerpiece of a trade involving Jhostynxon Garcia, one of Boston’s top prospects. The right-hander pounded the strike zone through 2 ⅓ innings, throwing 20 of his 30 pitches for strikes, generating three whiffs and four strikeouts.
John Holobetz dominated out of the bullpen, striking out eight Bulls and recording an absurd 20 whiffs while not allowing any runs over 4 ⅓ innings. Tyler Samaniego gave up a run in his lone inning, but with how miserable the offense looked, it did not seem to matter. Noah Song finished off the final 1 ⅓ innings, shutting out Durham with one strikeout and just one base runner allowed.
Standout Performances:
- Johan Oviedo: 2 ⅓ IP, 2 H, 1 ER, 1 BB, 4 K
- John Holobetz: 4 ⅓ IP: 2 H, 0 ER, 2 BB, 8 K

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Johan Oviedo Wants To Return In Any Role To Help Red Sox After Missing Nearly Entire Season
item.dc:creator: Aaliyan Mohammed
item.description: The Boston Red Sox acquired Johan Oviedo from the Pittsburgh Pirates in the winter, thinking he would be their No. 5 starter. However, Connelly Early won that job in spring training, and Oviedo was relegated to the bullpen. Near the end of spring training, his velocity was noticeably down, and he gave up six hits and four earned runs in his only outing for the Red Sox this year. He was placed on the injured list with an elbow sprain and pitched in a rehab game with Triple-A Worcester on Thursday
item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox acquired Johan Oviedo from the Pittsburgh Pirates in the winter, thinking he would be their No. 5 starter.
However, Connelly Early won that job in spring training, and Oviedo was relegated to the bullpen. Near the end of spring training, his velocity was noticeably down, and he gave up six hits and four earned runs in his only outing for the Red Sox this year. He was placed on the injured list with an elbow sprain and pitched in a rehab game with Triple-A Worcester on Thursday.
His velocity was back up, topping out at 98.5 mph and averaging 95.9 mph with his fastball. That is where the Red Sox expected him to be when they got him. The Red Sox could use a starter right now, but just like Garrett Crochet, there is not time to get Oviedo built up as a starter.
"You always have great dreams about playing for a team like (Boston) with a lot of history," Oviedo said, per MassLive's Katie Morrison-O'Day. "You want to fill up your spot, and not being available to help the team from the beginning definitely has been a challenge for me. If I still have a shot to help the team in any way, in the last few weeks of the season or the playoffs, I'm just trying to be ready."
"I'm more than open to fill any role, and not finish the season on the IL," Oviedo added. "It's definitely not the plan for any pitcher. But all I'm trying to do right now is be healthy and be available for the team if they need me.
Oviedo pitched 2 1/3 innings on Thursday, notching four strikeouts. He gave up one run, two hits and a walk, landing 20 of his 30 pitches for strikes. He threw his four-seamer, slider, sinker, curveball and changeup in the outing.
Oviedo is a talented pitcher, and it's very possible that he would have been a staple in the rotation this year had he not gotten hurt. The minor league season is about to end, so there won't be many more opportunities for him to get rehab outings. He is unsure if he will be on the taxi squad or get to pitch for the Red Sox this year. However, he wants to be ready if his number is called.
"I've been on a playoff roster before but never pitched," Oviedo said. "So it's definitely one of the dreams that I want to accomplish. If Boston will give me that chance, if the team needs me, hopefully I can be ready for it."
More MLB: Red Sox's Caleb Durbin Provides Details On Injury He's Playing Through

item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox are getting ready for the postseason, and their starting third baseman has been playing hurt.
Caleb Durbin dislocated his pinky earlier in the year and then reinjured it. However, he has continued to play, swing a good bat, and play elite defense at third base. He received X-rays after the original injury and the reinjury, but he was told there was no fracture and he could play if he could handle the pain.
"It doesn't quite straighten or bend all the way," Durbin told the Boston Globe's Alex Speier.
Durbin started the season off terribly at the plate. However, since May 28, he is slashing .285/.371/.444 with 12 home runs and 28 total extra-base hits. He does not miss games, and has lived up to the reputation he built in Milwaukee.
"There really is kind of a joint understanding (with the team) that we'll get it looked at at the end of the season if we have to, because (whatever the diagnosis is), it's not going to impact my decision to play at all," he said.
Durbin said he is not sure if he will require surgery in the offseason, but for now, he is focused on helping the Red Sox win. The team was essentially headed for a lost season, but Chad Tracy has turned things around. Durbin turning his season around has also played a huge role in that.
More MLB: Red Sox's Willson Contreras Comments On Injury After X-Rays Show No Fracture

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Red Sox’s Willson Contreras in injury scare with Yankees’ wild-card showdown looming
item.dc:creator: Grace McCarron

item.content:encoded:
The Red Sox had a scare on Thursday night when Willson Contreras was hit by a pitch on his right hand in the eighth inning of Boston's 4-3 win over the Rangers.
Contreras was struck on a first-pitch sinker from Jakob Junis in the eighth inning. He walked to first base showing clear signs of pain before a trainer came to examine him and he went to the dugout. Just a couple of batters later, Trevor Story hit a go-ahead three-run home run to help the Sox avoid the sweep by Texas.
Postgame, interim manager Chad Tracy said Contreras's hand was bruised with a little swelling, but X-rays came back negative. Tracy said the team will "take it day to day" with Contreras.
As the regular season winds down, the Red Sox will have to manage their injuries in their pursuit of a deep October run. They open their weekend series against the red-hot Rays in Tampa on Friday night, possibly without their most consistent hitter.
Contreras said he probably won't play in the series opener.
Contreras told the Boston Globe he originally felt like he had fractured his hand, an injury he's experienced before.
"Sore. Painful. My hand was numb for like five minutes," Contreras said. "That was the reason I came out of the game. I have fractured, before, the same hand. It felt like a fracture. Thankfully, it's not a fracture on the top of the bone."
Contreras also expressed frustration over being frequently hit by pitches during his time in the big leagues. This season, Contreras ranks third in the majors in hit-by-pitches.
"If nobody does anything about it, I'm going to keep getting hit. That's the way I see it. That's it," he explained.
"I mean, sore bones in the hands — might take two days, might take a week, might take ten days. I don't know. We'll see how I feel after taking this plane to Tampa."
Should the Rays come out on top of the AL East, the Red Sox will likely face the Yankees in the AL Wild Card series, one in which they'll need their best hitters at 100% against one of the top pitching staffs in the league.

item.content:encoded:
Willson Contreras gets hit by a lot of pitches — he's been hit 24 times in 129 games this year, tying his career high — but the one on September 17 was different. Contreras mostly takes his base without issue, occasionally chirping pitchers and trying to rally his teammates on the way, but it was obvious something was wrong this time.
In the top of the eighth inning, a pitch from Texas Rangers pitcher Jakob Junis knocked Contreras in the hand. The first baseman hit the ground and immediately shook out his hand in pain. He walked off the field with a trainer uncharacteristically fast, which only worsened fans' nerves.
Postgame x-rays of Contreras' hand came back clear of any breaks but he's still experiencing pain (according to Chris Cotillo of MassLive). Contreras is less convinced by the results of the imaging. He told reporters he thinks his hand is fractured and that it went numb for a time after the hit (via Tim Healey of The Boston Globe).
The Red Sox have classified Contreras as day-to-day, but his reaction coupled with the club's history of evaluating injuries has some people doubting the diagnosis. The situation is reminiscent of what happened with Curtis Mead.
Willson Contreras' pain level seemingly outweighing initial diagnosis is giving Red Sox fans Curtis Mead flashbacks
A pitch plunked Mead on the wrist in his second at-bat as a Red Sox following the team's acquisition at the trade deadline. Initial imaging came back clear. The following day, he underwent a more detailed scan that revealed a wrist fracture. The fracture was non-displaced, meaning the broken part of his wrist remained aligned so he didn't have to undergo surgery to repair it, but his wrist is fractured all the same.
The Red Sox had better hope their initial diagnosis is correct this time. Losing Contreras for any amount of time, even with a day-to-day diagnosis, is a brutal outcome for the Sox. He's fresh off the injured list after a nearly two-week stint with a hamstring issue and he expects to be sidelined again for at least a few days.
Contreras has been Boston's most important bat all season and his career-high 27 home runs lead the team. The Red Sox need Contreras at his best for their playoff run, but if his hand is injured in any way, "his best" may be out the window.
Hopefully Contreras' initial diagnosis is right and Boston doesn't have another Mead situation on its hands. Contreras has been too important to the Red Sox's offense all season and his leadership is too valuable to lose him long-term at such a critical time, but the injury bug doesn't bite at ideal times.

item.title: [yanksgoyard.com] Sudden Aroldis Chapman injury issue adds uncertain wrinkle to Yankees-Red Sox showdown
item.dc:creator: Stephen Parello
item.description: The New York Yankees and Boston Red Sox seem destined for another October clash. You can smell the narrative building now. The Red Sox will be painted as the underdogs due to their horrid start to the season. Fine. Whatever makes them feel better. For the Yankees, this could be a tipping point, a chance to regain that sense of dominance over their hated rival. To that end, New York might have just gotten a piece of news that could further tip the scales in its favor, and it has to do old "friend
item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees and Boston Red Sox seem destined for another October clash. You can smell the narrative building now. The Red Sox will be painted as the underdogs due to their horrid start to the season. Fine. Whatever makes them feel better.
For the Yankees, this could be a tipping point, a chance to regain that sense of dominance over their hated rival. To that end, New York might have just gotten a piece of news that could further tip the scales in its favor, and it has to do old "friend" Aroldis Chapman.
After dropping the first two games of their series against the Texas Rangers, Boston mounted a late-inning comeback following a Trevor Story three-run homer in the eighth inning against Texas's all-world closer Jacob Latz. Coming out to secure the victory in the ninth wasn't Chapman, though; instead, it was another former Yankee, Garrett Whitlock. After the game, it was revealed that Chapman was "unavailable" because he's dealing with a sore lat.
Red Sox interim manager said that it's an issue that Chapman has been dealing with for a few days, and that the team will be conservative with his usage for the time being. The 38-year-old, who recently learned the importance of throwing strikes, has seen his command get spotty over his last two outings, issuing three walks in the process. Perhaps the injury is to blame?
Red Sox injury issues, including Aroldis Chapman, Willson Contreras, and others, could give Yankees the upper hand
At this point, it's unclear whether or not Chapman will need to head to the IL, but either way him being less than 100% bodes well for the Yankees. That will be especially true if he remains active and reverts to his wild ways in the upcoming playoff matchup.
Chapman isn't the only Boston player banged up, either. Willson Contreras was hit by a pitch on the hand during the Red Sox's win over the Rangers. X-rays were initially negative, but the former St. Louis Cardinal said he's suffered hand fractures before and that this felt the same way. He'll be sent for imaging and further tests to determine the true extent.
Contreras has been hit a total of 24 times this season, the third-most in baseball. He seems frustrated, too, saying that it will keep happening "if nobody does anything about it." Sounds like he's frustrated that Boston pitchers haven't come to his defense, threatening to cause an issue for the Red Sox even if his hand injury proves to be nothing serious.
That's not the end of the problems for the Red Sox. Roman Anthony, who missed nearly four months due to a torn finger ligament, is slumping hard. After an initial burst in his first two games back after being activated on August 30, Anthony has slashed just .200/.268/.338 thus far in September.
The biggest news of all, though, is Chapman. If he avoids the IL but is diminished, it could give the Yankees a key advantage in the most crucial moments of the expected matchup. The Sox's other primary bullpen lefty, Erik Miller, is also suffering from mechanical issues at a particularly brutal time. Capitalizing on that edge will be a must, and if the Red Sox fall to New York due to a Chapman postseason meltdown, the moment will be that much sweeter.

item.title: [Worcester Telegram] Kristian Campbell reflects on a rollercoaster 2026 season with WooSox
item.dc:creator: Tommy Cassell
item.description: Kristian Campbell reflects on a rollercoaster 2026 season with WooSox WORCESTER — Seated inside the Worcester Red Sox dugout Thursday afternoon, Kristian Campbell took stock of his 2026 season — while taking a break from the gray boot that’s occupied his left foot for the past few days. “It’s been pretty solid,” the soft-spoken Campbell told the T&G. “I mean, I learned a lot about myself.” A week prior, the 24-year-old outfielder landed on the 7-day injured list with a broken left toe, which eff
item.content:encoded:
Kristian Campbell reflects on a rollercoaster 2026 season with WooSox
WORCESTER — Seated inside the Worcester Red Sox dugout Thursday afternoon, Kristian Campbell took stock of his 2026 season — while taking a break from the gray boot that’s occupied his left foot for the past few days.
“It’s been pretty solid,” the soft-spoken Campbell told the T&G. “I mean, I learned a lot about myself.”
A week prior, the 24-year-old outfielder landed on the 7-day injured list with a broken left toe, which effectively ended his AAA season.
“He was a big part of what we’ve been doing,” WooSox acting manager Iggy Suarez said. “So, it’s definitely a downer for that.”
Path less traveled
As Campbell comes into Polar Park each day, the Worcester Red Sox player takes a unique route to the home clubhouse.
He enters through the parking lot located beyond the left-field wall, strolls through the blue seats in the stands, touches the warning track dirt for a few steps before walking down the stairs of the home dugout. It’s not a path many (if any) players take when arriving at the ballpark.
But like his journey inside the Red Sox organization for the past three seasons, Campbell’s taken the path less traveled. From High A to Triple A in 2024, to the big leagues and back to the minors last year, to spending his entire 2026 season in Triple A, it’s been an interesting course for the 6-foot-3, 210-pound Campbell.
“Everybody has their own journey,” Campbell told the T&G last year.
In the spring of 2025, Campbell impressed the Red Sox brass enough to garner a spot on Boston’s Opening Day roster and shortly after that he inked an eight-year, $60 million contract extension.
“It was the first time, I guess, that playing hard and just playing for the love of the game actually, literally, paid off,” Campbell said last season.
Boston saw dividends right away from calling up Campbell — and giving him a contract extension. He was named the American League Rookie of the Month for April after batting .301 with 4 home runs, 12 RBIs and a .902 OPS through his first 29 big-league games.
But then the struggles started for the then Red Sox rookie last year — at the plate (where he hit in every spot except leadoff and No. 2) and in the field (2B, CF, LF and DH). Starting on May 1, Campbell went into a prolonged slump in which he hit .159 with 2 homers, 9 RBIs and a .465 OPS across a 38-game stretch.
On June 20, 2025, Campbell was demoted to Triple-A Worcester. Nearly 15 months later, Campbell remains in AAA.
“In the moment, we certainly thought Kristian was ready and felt like he was going to hit the ground running and he did,” Red Sox senior director of player development Brian Abraham told the T&G this week. “But then, as the league had a better feel for him and found out his weaknesses, it was a little bit harder for him to adjust in the moment.
“So, I think it’s just a reminder that it’s really hard to not only have success, but to fail, then have success again,” Abraham added. “And making sure that we’re supporting him as much as we can (in) the day-to-day, making sure that the highs aren’t too high and the lows aren’t too low.”
Sticking to the plan
Although Campbell started slow to start his 2026 season, the right-handed hitter — with an athletic yet unorthodox swing — found his footing at the plate.
In July, Campbell hit .379 (22 for 58) with 2 HR and 11 RBIs.
“We’re starting to see him believing in himself again,” Suarez said at the time.
“To be able to work through some of the adversity and the struggles — (and) to get to a point this last couple of months where he was performing well, was, really cool to see,” Abraham said.
Through five games this month, Campbell was hitting .412 (7 for 17) with 1 HR, 5 RBIs and 4 walks. He saw the ball well and sprayed the ball all over the field — shades of his 2024 and early 2025 self.
“I think we were looking at someone who could’ve been in the mix for a potential call-up,” Abraham said. “But, obviously, that’s not in the cards anymore.”
During his third at-bat in a game against the Lehigh Valley IronPigs on Sept. 8, Campbell hit his foot with his bat on a follow-through from his swing. The result: a broken left toe.
He was placed on the 7-day IL two days later.
“It’s unfortunate,” Suarez said.
“It’s just part of baseball. Things happen,” Campbell said. “I just got to make sure I treat myself the right way and make sure this injury doesn't prolong. So, I’ll be good, sooner than later.”
Across 109 games and 371 at-bats, Campbell collected a .256 batting average with 8 HRs and 51 RBIs. His 2026 season was another case of Dr. Jekyll (second half) and Mr. Hyde (first half).
“(In the) first half (I was) trying stuff,” Campbell said. “(In the) second half (I was) sticking to (my) plan. That’s pretty much it, and that tells you two different things you get when you stick to your plan versus trying stuff. That’s how I think about it. And now I know exactly what makes me that type of player, so I’m going to stick to that.”
Back on the map
While Campbell has been sidelined this week in Worcester and the AAA club wraps up its regular season on Sunday, he continues to stick around and work out each day at Polar Park.
Campbell hopes to heal in time and stay ready as part of a Red Sox taxi squad in Fort Myers, Florida in case the Red Sox need reinforcements during the playoffs.
While a late season/postseason call up seems like a long shot at this point for Campbell, the former top Red Sox prospect has positioned himself to be in the conversation for another crack at Boston’s Opening Day roster in 2027.
“I think the guy we saw the last two months can compete with a lot of players in the big leagues to be a competitive and impactful player day in and day out in the lineup,” Abraham said. “So, obviously the work that he put in this year and the consistency needs to carry over into spring training, but I think he’s put himself in a position where he’s certainly back in those conversations, back on the map.
“And again, I don't think he was ever off (it), but to see the performance happen in real time in Worcester, not only just the hits and getting on base, but the actual under the radar, under the hood information that we value as well, were all trending up. So, definitely someone who’s going to be in those conversations as we head to spring next year.”
This year was another learning curve for Campbell. His baseball journey has been anything but linear over the past three years.
And as Campbell took stock of his 2026 season, the 24-year-old outfielder concluded with one final thought on his future.
“To be a Major League baseball player,” Campbell said. “I took this year to develop. But the future, it’s funny, I actually was thinking about that. More the mental side stuff for me. I like to focus on one day at a time. I don’t really think too much into the future, but obviously being a baseball player and knowing what I want to do, I do obviously want to be a Major League baseball player.
“I’m at the highest level and I’m going to keep working towards that. So, whenever I get the opportunity to do it, I’ll be ready.”
—Contact Tommy Cassell at tcassell@telegram.com. Follow him on X, formerly known as Twitter, @TommyCassell_.

item.dc:creator: Christopher Moore
item.description: The Boston Red Sox are expected to have to pay up to keep a star pitcher beyond 2026. At the moment, Sonny Gray’s future in Beantown is very much in the air. The three-time All-Star is currently in his final year under contract. The two sides do, however, have a $30 million mutual option to extend his stay in Boston another year. item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox are expected to have to pay up to keep a star pitcher beyond 2026. At the moment, Sonny Gray’s future in Beantown is very much in the air. The three-time All-Star is currently in his final year under contract. The two sides do, however, have a $30 million mutual option to extend his stay in Boston another year.
Despite this substantial salary, Gray would likely receive more money in the long term if he hit free agency. It was previously pointed out that the star would receive $10 million from the Red Sox if he declined the option. He could very well opt to collect the $10 million and then look for a lucrative multi-year deal elsewhere. If so, just how much money could the ace get in the winter?
Mass Live’s Chris Cotillo believes Gray could receive at least $75 million in the open market. “As a free agent, Gray’s renaissance season may position him to receive a lucrative deal that some in the industry expect to match or exceed the three-year, $75 million deal the Rangers gave to Nathan Eovaldi two winters ago,” writes Cotillo.
As the beat writer alludes to, Gray is experiencing a stellar campaign in his first season with the Boston Red Sox. The starter currently leads the American League with 17 wins and has posted a minuscule 2.82 ERA and 1.16 WHIP. Boston previously acquired the veteran in an offseason trade with the St. Louis Cardinals.
Boston Red Sox Hopeful Sonny Gray Returns to Team in 2027
While Gray could very well become a free agent, he has also recently admitted he is willing to return to the Boston Red Sox in 2027. As Cotillo reported, the pitcher claimed he was “definitely” open to signing an extension with the club. Craig Breslow, Boston’s president of baseball operations, will surely be looking to extend the star’s stay.
There is, however, a major wild card in all of this. Gray has recently hinted that he could very well retire soon. During a recent interview with The Boston Globe, the ace claimed that he would “be done in a heartbeat” if his family asked him to step away from the game.
Assuming the Boston Red Sox pitcher returns for his 15th MLB season and declines the mutual option, he should be positioned well in free agency, though. The upcoming starting pitching free agent class is not exactly super strong. Tarik Skubal is there, but Kevin Gausman and Freddy Peralta have seemingly hurt their values recently.
Boston Needs Star to Lead Team During Playoffs
For now, the Boston Red Sox will head towards the playoffs with Gray leading the way. Boston is currently in the fifth spot in the American League postseason standings. At the moment, they are projected to play against their bitter rivals, the New York Yankees, in the first round of the playoffs.
The veteran is likely to be the Boston Red Sox’s top starting pitcher during the upcoming postseason. The star leads the team’s rotation in wins, starts, innings, WAR, and ERA. He most recently allowed just three earned runs in six and a third innings during Boston’s victory on September 17.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Willson Contreras is ‘frustrated’ & calls out Red Sox
item.dc:creator: Matt Larter
item.description: The MLB season is heating up, and Boston Red Sox first baseman Willson Contreras is making it clear that he is frustrated with his own team after another painful hit-by-pitch. Contreras was forced to leave Boston's 4-3 win over the Texas Rangers on Thursday after being hit on the right hand by Rangers pitcher Jakob Junis in the eighth inning. The veteran infielder reportedly expressed his frustration after the game. "If nobody does anything about it, I'm going to keep getting hit," Contreras rep
item.content:encoded:
The MLB season is heating up, and Boston Red Sox first baseman Willson Contreras is making it clear that he is frustrated with his own team after another painful hit-by-pitch.
Contreras was forced to leave Boston's 4-3 win over the Texas Rangers on Thursday after being hit on the right hand by Rangers pitcher Jakob Junis in the eighth inning. The veteran infielder reportedly expressed his frustration after the game.
"If nobody does anything about it, I'm going to keep getting hit," Contreras reportedly said.
The 34-year-old finished the game 1-for-3 with a single, but the hit-by-pitch was particularly frustrating because it came just one night after he was also plunked by the Rangers. On Wednesday, Contreras was hit after launching a two-run home run during Boston's eventual 7-3 loss.
MORE: Yankees' Carlos Rodon sets franchise record
Contreras no stranger to getting hit
Aug 26, 2026; Miami, Florida, USA; Boston Red Sox first baseman Willson Contreras (40) looks on from inside the dugout against the Miami Marlins during the third inning at loanDepot Park. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)
Unfortunately for Contreras, getting hit by pitches is nothing new. He has developed a reputation for crowding the plate, and in 2020, he led the league in hit-by-pitches.
The latest incident is especially concerning because Contreras had only recently returned to Boston's lineup after spending time on the Injured List with a hamstring strain. He suggested that his latest injury could take up to 10 days to recover from.
There was some good news for the Red Sox. Initial X-rays reportedly showed no fracture, meaning Contreras and Boston appear to have avoided a potentially serious injury. Still, the first baseman described the pain as significant.
A key player for Boston's playoff push
Jul 22, 2026; Boston, Massachusetts, USA; Boston Red Sox first baseman Willson Contreras (40) hits a double against the Baltimore Orioles during the fourth inning at Fenway Park. Mandatory Credit: Brian Fluharty-Imagn Images
Contreras has been an important offensive contributor for Boston this season, batting .276 with 27 home runs through 129 games. He has also been hit by a pitch 24 times, matching his career high from the 2022 season with the Chicago Cubs.
With the Red Sox battling for a postseason spot, keeping Contreras healthy will be crucial. Boston currently holds the second American League Wild Card position and has a five-game cushion over the Cleveland Guardians.
The Red Sox will begin a three-game weekend series against the Tampa Bay Rays on Friday, with Contreras' health likely to be something worth watching closely.

item.title: [Sportsnaut] MLB Rumors: Insider Reveals Potential Cost of New Sonny Gray Contract, Disaster Scenario for Red Sox

item.description: Boston Red Sox starting pitcher Sonny Gray has been one of the best hurlers in baseball this season, entering the weekend in the mix to win the American League Cy Young Award. While he’ll likely be pitching in October for Boston, keeping him long-term reportedly could be an issue. MassLive.com‘s Chris Cotillo reports that Gray could command a three-year contract this winter, potentially in the range of $75 million total. It would be closely aligned to what Nathan Eovaldi received in December 202
item.content:encoded:
Boston Red Sox starting pitcher Sonny Gray has been one of the best hurlers in baseball this season, entering the weekend in the mix to win the American League Cy Young Award. While he’ll likely be pitching in October for Boston, keeping him long-term reportedly could be an issue.
MassLive.com‘s Chris Cotillo reports that Gray could command a three-year contract this winter, potentially in the range of $75 million total. It would be closely aligned to what Nathan Eovaldi received in December 2024 with the Texas Rangers.
The project salary for Gray is fairly reasonable given how well he’s performed on the mound this season. At a $25 million average annual value, he would be tied for 17th among the highest-paid starting pitchers in MLB.
Given the financial flexibility that Boston has, it should be a reasonable price to tack onto the Red Sox payroll in 2027. However, Cotillo also wrote that Gray disclosed in an interview with The Boston Globe that the 36-year-old will retire “in a heartbeat” if his family wants him to step away from baseball and be around them more.
Gray will turn 37 years old in November and he’s already pulled in more than $125 million in career MLB earnings, according to Spotrac.com. The Tennessee native has a home in Nashville, where his wife and their two children reside. He’s reportedly spent his off days visiting them and, per Cotillo, the Red Sox organization believes retirement is a real possibility.
If Gray retires, that creates an immediate void in the Red Sox rotation ahead of an MLB free agency class that is not particularly deep when it comes to proven starting pitchers. Assuming Tarik Skubal is outside of Boston’s price range, Trevor Rogers and Freddy Peralta are the top options expected to be available.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Red Sox's Willson Contreras Voices Frustration With Volume Of Hit By Pitches
item.dc:creator: Aaliyan Mohammed
item.description: Boston Red Sox first baseman Willson Contreras was hit in the hand by a pitch on Thursday and exited the game early. Contreras has been hit by a pitch 24 times this year, ranking third in all of baseball. He has been known for getting hit a lot throughout his career, but this year marks a new career best. Obviously, it's not a fun experience, and Contreras is getting kind of tired of it. "A lot of people might say that I hit on top of the plate, but I'm seeing a lot of players hit on top of the
item.content:encoded:
Boston Red Sox first baseman Willson Contreras was hit in the hand by a pitch on Thursday and exited the game early.
Contreras has been hit by a pitch 24 times this year, ranking third in all of baseball. He has been known for getting hit a lot throughout his career, but this year marks a new career best. Obviously, it's not a fun experience, and Contreras is getting kind of tired of it.
"A lot of people might say that I hit on top of the plate, but I'm seeing a lot of players hit on top of the plate. They don't get hit like me," Contreras said after the game, per The Boston Globe's Tim Healey. "It's really frustrating because I just came back from the IL (because of a hamstring strain), and this might take days. I mean, sore bones in the hands — might take two days, might take a week, might take 10 days."
The most frustrating part is that the Red Sox don't have much runway left for him to heal. The regular season is almost over, and the Red Sox will need Contreras in the wild card round.
X-rays were negative for Contreras, according to Chad Tracy, but as fans have seen this year, that does not mean he is in the clear. He will likely get additional imaging done.
"It felt like a fracture," Contreras said. "I'm just frustrated."
More MLB: Dodgers Magic Number: How Close Are Dodgers To Securing Bye After Winning NL West?

item.title: [MassLive.com] Johan Oviedo hopes to ‘have a shot to help the [Red Sox]’ any way he can
item.dc:creator: Katie Morrison-O’Day; Kamorrison

item.content:encoded:
WORCESTER -- Johan Oviedo is racing against the clock to get back and help the Red Sox.
Making his first rehab start since hitting the injured list on April 3 with a flexor sprain in his right elbow, Oviedo topped out at 98.5 mph with his sinker and went 2 1/3 innings.
The righty allowed one run on two hits and a walk, striking out four. The three swings and misses he recorded came on his four-seamer.
He was efficient, using 30 pitches to reach the third inning.
“(I was) super excited to get the first one out,” Oviedo said. “I just feel blessed, and hopefully I can continue to get healthy.”
Oviedo averaged just under 96 mph with both his four-seamer and his sinker, but said he wasn’t worried about what the radar was reading.
“Velo has never really been a concern,” Oviedo said. “It’s more about health-wise, how the arm feels. It’s more about making sure that my body moves well. If the body’s moving well, I know the velo will be there. But I mean, it’s always a good sign to see good velo on the radar.”
Oviedo was acquired by the Red Sox in December in a five-player deal that sent Jhostynxon Garcia to the Pirates. He only got to make one appearance before landing on the injured list in April.
“You always have great dreams about playing for a team like (Boston) with a lot of history,” Oviedo said. “You want to fill up your spot, and not being available to help the team from the beginning definitely has been a challenge for me. If I still have a shot to help the team in any way, in the last few weeks of the season or the playoffs, I’m just trying to be ready.”
Primarily a starter throughout his career, it’s possible Oviedo may not have enough time to stretch out as a starter before the Red Sox need him, and he says he’s open to however the team could use him.
“I’m more than open to fill any role, and not finish the season on the IL,” Oviedo said. “It’s definitely not the plan for any pitcher. But all I’m trying to do right now is be healthy and be available for the team if they need me.
Oviedo is no stranger to rehabbing; he missed all of 2024 after undergoing Tommy John surgery but returned to make nine starts with a 3.57 ERA in 2025.
“(There were) definitely a lot of feelings,” Oviedo said about making his first appearance in a game in months. “But as a professional, you’re trying to keep everything under control, put your feelings in balance. In the past, on the first outing, you [might] try to do more than what you can do. So today I was trying to keep it the same, treat it like another live BP in Florida.”
Oviedo is running out of days to pitch in games as he tries to get back to the major-league team, as the WooSox’ season ends on Sunday and the opportunity for in-game rehab outings ends with it. The pitcher said he wasn’t aware of what the plan was going forward and whether he’d be part of the Red Sox’ taxi squad.
With nine games left in the Red Sox’ season, there’s a chance the next time Oviedo is with the team is in the postseason,
“I’ve been on a playoff roster before but never pitched,” Oviedo said. “So it’s definitely one of the dreams that I want to accomplish. If Boston will give me that chance, if the team needs me, hopefully I can be ready for it.”
Notes
- Braiden Ward, who has been a topic of conversation since Red Sox manager Chad Tracy brought up his name as a potential late-season call-up, stole his 60th base of the season on Wednesday. Ward leads the International League in stolen bases and holds the WooSox record in steals. He’s 60-for-69 (87%) on attempts this season.
“Speed kills, and it never slumps,” WooSox manager Iggy Suarez said. “Any time you have speed like that, it can change the game; it can be a pain.”
- Tanner Houck is set to pitch for the WooSox again on Saturday after striking out the side in an inning of work on Tuesday for Worcester.
Performance of the Week
As the season winds down for Worcester, Allan Castro is heating up. The outfielder has bashed five home runs in 15 games this month, including two multi-home-run games over the last week. Castro’s two home runs and four RBI propelled the WooSox to a come-from-behind win on Wednesday.
Castro’s hot streak boosts his season slash line to .251/.325/.387 with 16 doubles, 14 home runs, and a triple.
What’s Next
The 2026 season wraps up over the weekend with three final games against the Durham Bulls. Sunday will feature a pre-game meet-the-team autograph party.
The WooSox aren’t officially eliminated from postseason contention, but need a whole lot to go right for them to clinch over the three teams currently above them in the standings with three games to go.

Contreras stepped up to the plate in the eighth inning on Thursday night and was hit on the top of the hand and was in clear discomfort right away and quickly exited the game and was replaced by Isiah Kiner-Falefa as a pinch runner. After the game, C
item.content:encoded:
If the Boston Red Sox are going to make a deep playoff run this season, they're going to need first baseman Willson Contreras at his best. Unfortunately, he is up in the air rigth now after leaving Thursday's contest early against the Texas Rangers.
Contreras stepped up to the plate in the eighth inning on Thursday night and was hit on the top of the hand and was in clear discomfort right away and quickly exited the game and was replaced by Isiah Kiner-Falefa as a pinch runner.
After the game, Contreras shared an update about the injury, as transcribed by MassLive.com's Chris Cotillo.
"Sore. Painful," Contreras said. "My hand was numb for like five minutes. That was the reason I came out of the game. I have fractured, before, the same hand. It felt like a fracture. Thankfully, it’s not a fracture on the top of the bone. I’m just frustrated."
When your most consistent hitter has any sort of injury scare with under two weeks to go until the playoffs, that's something that warrants some nerves in the fanbase, especially when the offense has been struggling. The fact that he specifically said that he had a fracture before and that it felt the same added to the fears. On the bright side, he underwent an X-ray that initially came back negative. Still, he's not fully out of the water yet.
Best-Case Scenario
In a perfect world, the pain subsides for Contreras and he's able to return to the field on Friday night on the road against the Tampa Bay Rays with just a bruise. Or, at the very least, he's able to play at some point during the series against Tampa Bay.
It's not hard to see why this would be the best-case scenario. Contreras has played in 129 games and is slashing .276/.387/.518 with a .905 OPS, 27 homers, 81 RBIs, and 21 doubles. Plus, he's at 4.6 wins above replacement. The quicker he can get back, the better. He already underwent an X-ray that had good news. Now, it all comes down to how it feels when he wakes. Hopefully, when the swelling goes down, it doesn't reveal any more issues.
Worst-Case Scenario
For the worst-case scenario, look no further than Curtis Mead. When Mead initially got hit by a pitch on his hand back in July, his X-rays initially came back negative. Then, after further testing, it was revealed that he actually suffered a fractured wrist. Mead hasn't played in a game since and it's unclear if the Red Sox will get him before the season comes to a close.
The worst-case scenario for Contreras would be something similar happening. As the swelling goes down, if it were to reveal some sort of fracture as well, that would be bad news for his chances of a quick return.

Got him on the top hand as he turned through on his right hand. So some swelling, and we'll just take it day to day.” Wilyer Ab
item.content:encoded:
ARLINGTON – Red Sox first baseman Willson Contreras exited Thursday’s 4-3 win against the Rangers after being hit by a pitch on his right hand in the eighth inning. X-rays were negative, and Contreras is considered day to day.
“He's got a bruise on his hand and some swelling,” interim manager Chad Tracy said postgame. “So we'll just take it day to day and see how he is. Got him on the top hand as he turned through on his right hand. So some swelling, and we'll just take it day to day.”
Wilyer Abreu worked a six-pitch walk to lead off the frame before Contreras was struck on the hand by a 92.3 mph sinker from Jakob Junis.
Contreras went to the ground in pain before getting back to his feet and making his way toward first base, where Abreu helped steady him. Tracy and a member of the training staff emerged from the dugout, and Contreras left the game shortly after.
“[It’s feeling] sore, painful,” Contreras said. “My hand was numb for like, I'll say five minutes. That was the reason why I came out of the game. I had fractures before in the same hand. It felt like a fracture. Thankfully, it was not a fracture on the top of the bone. … I don’t know, I'm just frustrated.”
The injury scare came just four days after Contreras was activated from the 10-day IL. He had been sidelined since Aug. 31 with a left hamstring strain before returning to Boston’s lineup Sunday against the Royals.
“[Junis] apologized to me. I mean, that was nice of him,” Contreras said. “He was trying to pitch inside like everybody else. A lot of people might say that I hit on top of the plate, but I'm seeing a lot of players [that] hit on top of the plate. They don't get hit like me.
“It's really frustrating because I just came back from [the IL], and this might take days. I mean, sore bones in hands might take two days, might take a week, might take 10 days. I don't know. We'll see how I feel after taking this plane to Tampa.”
The 34-year-old said he was unsure whether he would be able to play Friday as the Red Sox open a three-game series against the Rays.
“If nobody [does] anything about it, I am going to keep getting hit,” Contreras said. “That’s the way I see it. That’s it.”
Contreras has set career highs in home runs (27), RBIs (81) and OPS+ (155 entering Thursday) in his first season with Boston. He hit a two-run homer in Wednesday's loss to the Rangers, the 199th home run of his career.

item.content:encoded:
Red Sox news: Aroldis Chapman dealing with concerning injury with playoffs approaching appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
In signature 2026 Boston Red Sox fashion, they rallied late and completed a comeback from three runs down against the Texas Rangers after they scored three runs in the eighth to take a 4-3 lead they would not relinquish. But even with the Red Sox facing a save situation in the bottom of the ninth, it wasn't closer Aroldis Chapman who came off the bullpen to shut the door on the Rangers.
Red Sox interim manager Chad Tracy rolled with Garrett Whitlock in the bottom of the ninth, and Whitlock responded with a save, improving Boston to 83-70 on the season. After the game, Tracy revealed that Chapman wasn't available on the night anyway as the hard-throwing lefty is currently dealing with a "lat issue", as per Tim Healey of the Boston Globe.
Tracy added that the Red Sox are going to be "conservative" with utilizing Chapman off the pen to end the regular season, as keeping him healthy for the postseason is going to be important for this team.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
Chapman last made an appearance for the Red Sox on the 13th of September in a 4-1 win over the Kansas City Royals. While he did allow two walks in that save situation, he made up for it by striking the side, making it look as though he wasn't dealing with any injury.
Nonetheless, the Red Sox, now armed with a seven-game cushion over the AL Wild Card cutoff line, have the luxury anyway to bring Chapman along slowly.
The Red Sox also have other injury matters to deal with. According to Healey, Tracy also said that first baseman Willson Contreras, who recently returned to the lineup (returning on September 13 against the Royals), is dealing with a bruised right hand and is currently day-to-day. The good news for Boston is that his X-rays turned out negative.
With the Red Sox on the cusp of sealing a postseason spot, they can afford to do whatever it takes to keep their core players healthy so that they can trot out their best squad come postseason time.

item.content:encoded:
The Chicago Cubs were off on Thursday. That doesn't mean they didn't have something to win.
With the team about to begin a road series against the Cincinnati Reds, the entire roster seemingly opted to hop the Ohio-Kentucky border and travel to Churchill Downs, where Alex Bregman's horse Act of Parliament was competing in the final race of the slate.
Act of Parliament won a thriller, starting near the back of the park and slowly making up ground on the outside, then erasing a length-plus gap in the final stretch for the win.
You can see the team cheering him on here, via video from trainer William Walden:
The Cubs players were fully invested. Bregman posting pictures on his Instagram story of multiple teammates wearing jockey uniforms on the team plane, as well as video of Pete Crow-Armstrong meeting the horse before the race with the caption "PCA pep talk we couldn't lose," which can only help the MVP campaign.
The team celebrated raucously after Act of Parliament crossed the finish line, later hoisting jockey Axel Concepcion on their shoulders.
Via MLB.com, Bregman has been a horse racing fan his entire life, something he takes from his family, and made a formal entry into the world when he opened Bregman Family Racing in 2021 alongside his wife Reagan, who also grew up racing horses.
Bregman Family Racing has seen its horses record a total of 90 starts since then.
Act of Parliament's win paid out $8.68 off a $2 bet to win and earned Bregman a $27,108 prize per Bloodhorse.
However, that appears to be the end of Bregman's association with the horse, as it was a maiden claiming race, in which all of the horses were up for immediate sale. According to Equibase, Act of Parliament was one of five horses claimed by a new set of owners at a price of $20,000 each.
With a horse racing win under their belt, the Cubs have nine games left to play in the regular season. Their record currently sits at 85-68, tied with the Philadelphia Phillies for the top wild-card spot (Chicago owns the tiebreaker) and have a five-game cushion over the Arizona Diamondbacks to make the playoffs.
If the playoff picture holds, they will host the Phillies in the NL wild-card round.

item.content:encoded:
Chapman day to day as Red Sox monitor lat tightness
This browser does not support the video element.
ARLINGTON -- Red Sox closer Aroldis Chapman was unavailable to pitch in Boston’s 4-3 win over the Rangers on Thursday at Globe Life Field due to lat tightness and is considered day to day.
“We're going to be conservative with [it],” interim manager Chad Tracy said postgame. “It's getting better, but we're going to make sure it gets there. That's why he wasn't available tonight.”
According to Tracy, Chapman has been dealing with the tightness for the last couple of days, so the team will continue to evaluate him.
“Obviously, you guys know how diligent he is about his prep and getting in and getting treatment. So we'll just monitor it day to day,” Tracy said.
On Thursday, Garrett Whitlock came in to close out the game, getting a groundout to first, issuing a walk and inducing a 6-4-3 double play to end it.
“[Whitlock is] great,” Tracy said. “He's reliable. He's done it before. If Chappie's down, he's very reliable in any spot we put him in.”
Through 51 games, Chapman owns a 1.95 ERA and a 1.14 WHIP, with hitters batting .190 against him. His 34 saves are tied for third in the AL and tied for fifth in the Majors. He is MLB’s all-time leader in relief strikeouts with 1,399.
Chapman’s absence Thursday was the latest injury concern for a Red Sox team that has had to rely on its depth throughout the season, with eight pitchers currently on the IL. Despite the injuries, Chapman has been impressed by the way younger players have responded when given opportunities.
This browser does not support the video element.
“They’ve come in because of all the injuries we’ve had, and they’ve been able to do an excellent job,” Chapman said in Spanish on Wednesday. “Now, some players have also returned from their injuries, but because of their youth and the limited playing time they’ve had, they’re doing a very good job with what has been asked of them.
“We always keep playing until the end because you never know what can happen, but [to see that from them] keeps me positive all the time.”

item.title: [MassLive.com] Why was Aroldis Chapman unavailable for Red Sox in win? Chad Tracy explains injury

That’s because one of them was unavailable due to a nagging — and previously undisclosed — injury. item.content:encoded:
ARLINGTON, Texas — When Trevor Story hit his clutch three-run homer to flip a two-run deficit into a one-run lead Thursday against the Rangers, interim manager Chad Tracy didn’t rush to get his two highest-leverage bullpen arms instantly ready. That’s because one of them was unavailable due to a nagging — and previously undisclosed — injury.
With Boston suddenly up, 4-3, Tracy used a pair of rookies (righty Wyatt Olds and lefty Alec Gamboa) to pitch the eighth, then turned things over to righty Garrett Whitlock in the ninth. For at least one night, Whitlock took the job of closer Aroldis Chapman, who has a tight lat muscle.
“He’s just dealing with some lat tightness we’re going to be conservative with,” Tracy said. “It’s getting better, but we’ve got to make sure it gets there. That’s why he wasn’t available tonight.”
Tracy said Chapman — who last pitched Saturday against the Royals — has been dealing with the injury for “a couple of days.” Asked if an injured list stint was possible for the All-Star, Tracy said: “We’re not doing that right now.”
“We’re just going to keep monitoring it and see where he’s at each day,” Tracy said. “Obviously, you know how diligent he is about his prep and getting in and getting treatment, so we’re just monitoring day-to-day.”
Chapman, 38, has had another stellar season in Boston, tallying 34 saves to go along with a 1.95 ERA and 68 strikeouts in 50 ⅔ innings over 52 games. He was one of two key Red Sox players with an injury concern Thursday; first baseman Willson Contreras left the game in the eighth inning after being hit on top of his right hand with a pitch.
Olds, who has a 1.23 ERA and 19 strikeouts in his first 12 MLB appearances since debuting last month, relieved Sonny Gray with one out in the seventh inning and the Sox trailing by two. He got two quick outs before Story’s three-run blast put Boston up 4-3. Olds got Ezequiel Duran to pop out to start the eighth before Gamboa entered for the left-on-left matchup against Corey Seager. Seager singled but Gamboa got Josh Jung to ground into an inning-ending double play five pitches later.
“They were awesome,” Tracy said. “Getting thrust into a big spot, going back out anyways, and then all of the sudden you’re going out with a lead. They did an amazing job.”
Whitlock then recorded his fourth save of the year, needing 12 pitches and getting a similar 6-4-3 double play to end the game.
“He’s great,” Tracy said. “He’s reliable. He’s done it before if Chappy’s down.”

item.content:encoded:
Boston Red Sox third baseman Caleb Durbin dislocated his left pinky in late June. He reinjured it early last month.
Before the Red Sox’s upcoming series against the Tampa Bay Rays at Tropicana Field, Durbin told the Boston Globe’s (subscription required) Alex Speier his pinky is still bothering him.
Boston Red Sox 3B Caleb Durbin Makes Statement on Injury Before Rays series
Durbin said his pinky doesn’t “quite straighten or bend all the way.”
The third baseman received X-Rays after he initially injured his pinky in June and after he reinjured it in August. Both times, the X-rays revealed there was no fracture.
“There really is kind of a joint understanding [with the team] that we’ll get it looked at at the end of the season if we have to, because [whatever the diagnosis is], it’s not going to impact my decision to play at all,” Durbin said.
Speier asked Durbin if he needs offseason surgery.
“I don’t know yet. We’ll find out,” he said. “I hope there’s something we can do about it. But we’ll get there when the time comes.”
Read More: Pinkie injury may be affecting Caleb Durbin, but it’s not keeping him out of Red Sox lineup
Despite his pinky injury, Durbin hasn’t been placed on the injured list at all this season.
Looking at Boston Red Sox 3B Caleb Durbin
On Feb. 9, the Red Sox acquired Durbin, shortstop Andruw Monasterio, second baseman Anthony Seigler and future considerations from the Milwaukee Brewers for second baseman David Hamilton and left-handers Kyle Harrison and Shane Drohan.
Durbin, 26, has hit .248/.333/.381 with 13 home runs and 64 RBI over 145 games with Boston this year.
Durbin made his MLB debut with the Brewers last season. He hit .256/.334/.387 with 11 home runs and 53 RBI during his rookie year.
The Red Sox will begin their series against the Rays at 7:10 p.m. EDT on Friday.

item.dc:creator: Matt Gross
item.description: This is why we watch! Trevor Story's season looked dead and buried both three months and three weeks ago.
