item.content:encoded:
This is why we watch! Trevor Story's season looked dead and buried both three months and three weeks ago. He's battled injury, surgery, rehab, way too many strikeouts, and growing chatter from knuckleheads like me who have repeatedly questioned if he even belongs back in this lineup.
Well tonight, he came to the plate with the Sox down 3-1 in the eighth and on the verge of getting swept. He was facing a tough reliever in Jacob Latz, a Texas team that was 63-1 when leading after seven innings, and the weight of his team going a combined 0-17 with runners in scoring position in the series up to that point.
Then he did this:
As somebody that's been leading the "Trevor Story is cooked " charges, I love this so much! Nothing can humble and amaze quite like baseball, and after months of hard work, grinding behind the scenes, and having to deal with all the noise, Story smashed a 108mph line drive home run not only in the face of Latz and Texas' playoff hopes, but also in the face of all those who have been doubting him for weeks (hand raised).
It's just one game, and the real test doesn't start until the 29th, but boy did this have to feel incredible for Story who hadn't gone deep since May 13th. To do it in that moment, in his home town, and against the backdrop of everything that's happened this year is just so perfectly baseball. It's why we love this game so much, and why people like Story are willing to put in the work behind the scenes for months on end to get the chance to do something amazing like that.
I know some of you might not believe it after what I've written about him in recent weeks, but I truly am very happy for Story! He deserves all the credit tonight!
Oh, and in addition to Story's game changing three-run homer, he followed that up by starting double plays on defense to end both the eighth and ninth:
Baseball really is the best!
Studs
Trevor Story: If I didn't put him here, I'd have to legally resign from Over The Monster.
Wilyer Abreu: He looked a little better tonight with a sharp single in the fourth and a walk that turned into a run on Story's three-run shot.
The bullpen: The comeback wouldn't be complete without the pen holding it down, and with Aroldis Chapman unavailable with lat tightness, Wyatt Olds, Alec Gamboa, and Garrett Whitlock combined to go 2.2 scoreless innings.
Duds
Only one dud tonight, and that's me given my recent stance on Story's playing time. The crow is delicious, and I hope it remains on the menu well into October!
One other important note
Just before Story's home run, Willson Contreras was hit in the hand by a pitch and had to leave the game. The good news is x-rays were negative, but given x-rays were also negative after Curtis Mead got hit in July, I'm not going to be celebrating this one until we get further confirmation.
X-rays were negative on Willson Contreras, at least initially, but he remains sore.
Aroldis Chapman was unavailable due to lat tightness and is day-to-day.
Willson Contreras: "Sore. Painful. My hand was numb for like five minutes. That was the reason I came out of the game. I have fractured, before, the same hand. It felt like a fracture. Thankfully, it’s not a fracture on the top of the bone. I’m just frustrated."
— Chris Cotillo (@ChrisCotillo) September 18, 2026
Play of the game:
Was there ever any doubt it would be Story's home run? Here's the game changing swing one more time.

item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox removed first baseman Willson Contreras from Thursday’s 4-3 win against the Texas Rangers at Globe Life Field in Arlington, Texas, after he was hit in the hand by a 92.3 mph sinker from Jakob Junis in the eighth inning.
Following the game, Red Sox manager Chad Tracy said that Contreras suffered a bruised right hand and is day to day.
From Tim Healy of the Boston Globe on X: Willson Contreras has a bruised right hand, Chad Tracy said. He is day to day. X-rays were negative.
Contreras was asked about the injury after the game.
Boston Red Sox 1B Willson Contreras Makes Statement on Injury Following Win Over Rangers
Via Chris Cotillo on X: Willson Contreras: “Sore. Painful. My hand was numb for like five minutes. That was the reason I came out of the game. I have fractured, before, the same hand. It felt like a fracture. Thankfully, it’s not a fracture on the top of the bone. I’m just frustrated.”
Contreras went 1-for-3 with a single and a strikeout in Thursday’s win.
The Red Sox acquired Contreras from the St. Louis Cardinals over the offseason. He is under contract through 2027 and has a 2028 club option worth $20 million.
Contreras, 34, is having a spectacular first season with Boston, slashing .276/.387/.518 with 27 home runs and 81 RBI over 129 games.
Recapping Boston’s 4-3 Win Over Rangers
Trevor Story hit a three-run home run in the eighth inning as the Red Sox beat the Rangers 4-3 on Thursday.
Sonny Gray allowed three earned runs on three hits and three walks while striking out six over 6 1/3 innings.
Rangers designated hitter Josh Jung hit a solo home run in the first inning, giving Texas a 1-0 lead.
Danny Jansen hit an RBI single in the second inning. Evan Carter followed with an RBI sac bunt, increasing the Rangers’ lead to 3-0.
The Red Sox scored their first run of the game on a throwing error from Nicky Lopez in the second inning. Then Story delivered the big hit in the eighth inning.
The Rangers used seven pitchers in the game. Cody Bradford pitched the most of any of them, hurling 4 1/3 scoreless innings.

item.content:encoded:
Trevor Story hit a three-run homer in the eighth inning as the Boston Red Sox overcame a three-run deficit to defeat the Texas Rangers 4-3 on Thursday in Arlington, Texas.
Story’s blast came against Texas closer Jacob Latz (3-3) and erased a 3-1 deficit.
The victory allowed Boston (83-70) to avoid being swept in the three-game series and ended the Rangers’ four-game winning streak. Josh Jung hit a solo home run for Texas (76-77), which fell a game behind the Houston Astros (77-76) at the top of the American League West.
Wyatt Olds (2-0) earned the win by tossing one scoreless inning. Boston starter Sonny Gray allowed three runs on three hits in 6 1/3 innings. He struck out six and walked three.
Texas had the tying run on first with one out in the ninth, but Garrett Whitlock got Jake Burger to ground into a game-ending double play for his fourth save.
Danny Jansen had two of the Rangers’ four hits, including an RBI single.
Boston’s Willson Contreras left the game after he was hit by a pitch on his right hand in the eighth inning. Contreras leads the Red Sox with 27 home runs.
Jung hit a solo shot in the first inning to open the scoring. It was his 10th homer of the season.
Texas extended its lead to 3-0 in the third. After two walks and a sacrifice bunt, Jansen singled home Wyatt Langford, and Burger scored on Evan Carter’s sacrifice bunt.
The Red Sox got on the scoreboard in the seventh. Nate Eaton and Caleb Durbin walked, and Eaton took third on a flyout. A throwing error by second baseman Nicky Lopez on Roman Anthony’s grounder brought in Eaton.
In the eighth, Boston’s Wilyer Abreu walked and Contreras was hit by a Jakob Junis pitch. Latz entered and got Adley Rutschman to foul out before Story belted a 2-2 curveball to left-center, handing Boston a 4-3 lead. It was Story’s fourth homer of the year.
The Boston offense struggled in the first two games of the series. The Red Sox struck out 15 times as the Rangers won 4-2 on Tuesday, and the visitors were held to three hits in a 7-3 loss on Wednesday.
–Field Level Media

item.content:encoded:
Story reaparece con jonrón y completa remontada de los Medias Rojas
This browser does not support the video element.
ARLINGTON -- Trevor Story esperó más de cuatro meses para conectar su siguiente jonrón. Y llegó justo a tiempo para los Medias Rojas.
Story finalmente despertó con un cuadrangular de tres carreras que puso a Boston al frente en el octavo inning la noche del jueves, impulsando a los Medias Rojas a una victoria por 4-3 sobre los Rangers en el Globe Life Field y ayudándolos a evitar su primera barrida desde julio.
Wilyer Abreu abrió el octavo episodio con una base por bolas antes de que Willson Contreras fuera golpeado por un lanzamiento y saliera del juego, con Isiah Kiner-Falefa ingresando como corredor emergente. Story entonces atacó una curva de 80.3 mph y la mandó en línea entre los jardines izquierdo y central para su primer vuelacercas desde el 13 de mayo y su cuarto de la temporada.
Boston había comenzado a reducir la desventaja un capítulo antes. Después de boletos consecutivos a Caleb Durbin y Nate Eaton, Roman Anthony bateó un rodado para una jugada forzada que permitió anotar a Eaton. Un error en tiro del segunda base Nicky López en la jugada permitió que Anthony avanzara a la intermedia.
La remontada en las últimas entradas llegó después de que Sonny Gray mantuviera a los Medias Rojas a una distancia alcanzable pese a un complicado comienzo de su apertura.
El derecho de 36 años lanzó 6.1 entradas, permitiendo tres carreras y tres hits, con seis ponches y tres bases por bolas en 102 pitcheos, su mayor cantidad de la temporada, de los cuales 67 fueron strikes.

item.content:encoded:
El primera base venezolano de Boston, Willson Contreras, salió del juego de los Medias Rojas la noche del jueves contra los Rangers de Texas en la octava entrada después de ser golpeado por un lanzamiento en la zona de la mano derecha.
Contreras recibió el impacto de una sinker al primer lanzamiento, lanzada por Jakob Junis, después de que el venezolano Wilyer Abreu negociara una base por bolas para abrir la entrada, con los Rangers arriba 3-1. Contreras caminó hacia la primera base con evidente dolor, fue revisado por un preparador físico del equipo y se dirigió al dugout.
Dos bateadores después, Trevor Story conectó un jonrón de tres carreras ante Jacob Latz.
Contreras iba 1 de 3, con un sencillo. Ya había sido golpeado por un lanzamiento la noche del miércoles, después de conectar un jonrón de dos carreras en la primera entrada de la derrota 7-3 de los Medias Rojas ante los Rangers.

item.content:encoded:
ARLINGTON, Texas (AP) — Trevor Story hit a three-run home run off All-Star closer Jacob Latz in the eighth inning, capping a comeback from a three-run deficit as the Boston Red Sox beat Texas 4-3 on Thursday night and dropped the Rangers out of the AL West lead.
Texas (76-77) had won four straight games to gain a share of the lead but dropped one game behind Houston (77-76), which holds the tiebreaker. The Rangers trail by two games for the last AL wild card.
Boston (83-70) has a five-game lead for the top AL wild card and improved to 8-59 when trailing after seven innings. Texas dropped to 63-2 when leading after seven innings.
Latz (3-3) entered after Wilyer Abreu walked starting the eighth and Willson Contreras was hit by a pitch from Jakob Junis.
Latz struck out Adley Rutschman and Story, who is from nearby Irving, reached down for Latz's second straight low curveball and drove the ball over the left-field wall for his fourth home run this season.
Boston’s Wyatt Olds (2-0) got three outs and Garrett Whitlock pitched the ninth for his fourth save in eight chances, getting Jake Burger to ground into a game-ending double play.
Josh Jung hit a first-inning homer off Sonny Gray, and Texas opened a 3-0 lead in the second on Danny Jansen's RBI single and Evan Carter's safety squeeze bunt.
Roman Anthony hit into a run-scoring forceout in the seventh.
Texas’ Cody Bradford followed a one-inning opener with 4 1/3 shutout innings, seeking his first major league since Sept. 18, 2024. He missed last season following elbow surgery.
Gray gave up three hits in 6 1/3 innings, throwing a season-high 102 pitches.
Up Next
Red Sox: LHP Ranger Suarez (7-4, 3.33) will go against LHP Ian Seymour (9-6, 4.27) on Friday at Tampa Bay.
Rangers: RHP Kumar Rocker (5-11, 4.54) starts Friday against visiting Toronto and RHP Dylan Cease (11-5, 2.38).

item.content:encoded:
Trevor Story Saves Red Sox From Crushing Sweep With One Swing originally appeared on NESN. Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
For seven innings, the Boston Red Sox appeared headed toward a disastrous conclusion to their stay in Texas.
Trevor Story changed everything with one swing.
Story crushed a three-run home run in the eighth inning Thursday night, lifting Boston to a dramatic 4-3 victory over the Texas Rangers at Globe Life Field. The comeback allowed the Red Sox to avoid a three-game sweep and improve to 83-70. Boston entered the seventh inning without a run and trailed 3-0. The Red Sox had managed only three hits through six innings and continued to waste the few scoring opportunities they generated.
Then the game suddenly flipped.
The Red Sox pushed across their first run in the seventh when Nate Eaton scored on a throwing error by Rangers second baseman Nicky Lopez. That cut the deficit to 3-1, but Boston still needed a much bigger response.
Story supplied it one inning later.
Trevor Story Delivers Red Sox's Biggest Swing
Wilyer Abreu opened the eighth with a single before Willson Contreras was hit by a pitch. Isiah Kiner-Falefa entered as a pinch runner, placing two runners aboard with one out.
Story then hammered Jacob Latz's offering 394 feet to left-center field.
The three-run blast turned a 3-1 deficit into a 4-3 advantage. It was Story's fourth home run of the season and accounted for three of Boston's four runs.
Story finished 2-for-4 and produced the Red Sox's only hit in seven at-bats with runners in scoring position. Boston recorded only five hits all night, making Story's timely power even more important.
The late rally rewarded starter Sonny Gray for keeping Boston close after a difficult beginning.
Texas scored once in the first inning on Josh Jung's solo home run before adding two more in the second. Gray settled down from there and held the Rangers scoreless over his final 4 1/3 innings. The veteran right-hander allowed three runs on three hits over 6 1/3 innings. He struck out six and walked three while throwing 102 pitches.
Red Sox Bullpen Protects One-Run Lead
Wyatt Olds recorded the final two outs of the seventh and returned for a scoreless eighth, earning his second victory of the season. Angel Gamboa completed the eighth before Garrett Whitlock handled the ninth. Whitlock issued a walk but did not allow a hit, securing his fourth save.
Boston's defense also turned two double plays, helping its pitching staff hold Texas to four hits.
The victory did not erase the disappointment of losing the first two games of the series. Texas still won the set after taking Monday's opener 4-2 and Tuesday's game 7-3.
It did, however, keep a frustrating trip from becoming a sweep at a critical point in the season.
For most of Thursday night, the Red Sox looked lifeless. Story needed only one pitch to completely rewrite the ending.

item.title: [Boston Herald] Trevor Story’s late home run helps Red Sox flip script on Rangers
item.dc:creator: Mac Cerullo
item.description: This has been a rough stretch for the Red Sox offense, which has effectively turned into a pumpkin after a torrid two months this summer. This week in particular the bats have fallen silent, and for much of Thursday night the Red Sox looked like they were headed toward a discouraging series sweep at the worst possible time. Things took an especially grim turn when Willson Contreras left the game in the eighth inning after being hit in the hand by a pitch, but while the specter of his absence wil
item.content:encoded:
This has been a rough stretch for the Red Sox offense, which has effectively turned into a pumpkin after a torrid two months this summer. This week in particular the bats have fallen silent, and for much of Thursday night the Red Sox looked like they were headed toward a discouraging series sweep at the worst possible time.
Things took an especially grim turn when Willson Contreras left the game in the eighth inning after being hit in the hand by a pitch, but while the specter of his absence will loom over the club in the days to come, Trevor Story once again proved that you can never count this Red Sox team out.
The veteran shortstop came through with a go-ahead three-run home run in the top of the eighth inning, flipping the script and giving the Red Sox a badly needed 4-3 win to avoid a sweep at the hands of the Texas Rangers.
Story’s shot came with one out against Rangers closer Jacob Latz, completing a three-run comeback and cutting Boston’s magic number to clinch a playoff spot to three with nine games remaining.
“To steal that last one is huge,” Story told NESN’s Jahmai Webster postgame. “It’s momentum we can ride out into Tampa.”
Prior to Story’s home run, Thursday was shaping up to be among the club’s worst losses of the season.
A hallmark of the offense’s struggles early in the year was a lot of empty, uncompetitive at-bats, tons of swing and miss and a general inability to make good contact. Even with the Rangers opting for a bullpen game led by Cody Bradford, whose fastball averages just 88.6 mph, the Red Sox couldn’t square anything up.
The Red Sox only managed two hits through the first five innings, both singles in the fourth inning. That put runners at the corners with two outs, but Jarren Duran grounded out to squander the opportunity.
It was a similar story in the sixth, when Wilyer Abreu singled and Adley Rutschman finally did some damage with a ground-rule double into the left-field gap. Had the ball stayed in play, Abreu probably would have scored, but instead the Red Sox had two men in scoring position for Story, who worked a full count and struck out to end the threat.
The offense did nothing to pick up Sonny Gray, who wasn’t perfect but did everything he could to keep the Red Sox in the game.
The veteran right-hander allowed a solo home run to Josh Jung with two outs in the first, and in the second he walked the first two batters of the inning, both of whom came around to score on an RBI bloop single by Danny Jansen and a run-scoring squeeze bunt by Evan Carter.
Gray settled down afterward and retired 14 of the last 16 batters he faced from the second inning into the seventh. He was charged with three runs over 6 1/3 innings and limited the Rangers to three hits and three walks with six strikeouts.
“I thought he was awesome,” Red Sox interim manager Chad Tracy said. “The only blemish was the two walks, we kind of walked ourselves into the part of their lineup where they can play baseball a little bit with bunts and they drop a flare into center and there’s a safety squeeze, outside of that, that was a really, really good effort.”
Even when the Red Sox finally scored in the top of the seventh, they did so without recording a hit. Nate Eaton and Caleb Durbin led off with consecutive walks and Eaton advanced to third after Nick Sogard hit a rocket of a fly out to the center field wall. But with one out and a chance to fight back into the game, Roman Anthony grounded into a run-scoring fielder’s choice to make it 3-1. He advanced to second after the Rangers threw away the double-play attempt, but Mickey Gasper grounded out to end the inning.
Then came the eighth.
Once again the Red Sox got two men on base right away, with Abreu drawing a leadoff walk before Contreras was hit in the right hand by a pitch. He immediately left the game with the trainer and was replaced at first by Isiah Kiner-Falefa, but while the Red Sox worried about their slugger, the Rangers pulled Jakob Junis for their closer Latz, who has been among the most dominant closers in the American League this year.
Latz drew a pop out from Rutschman, but then Story stepped up to the plate and everything changed.
“You see one of our guys keeled over holding his hand and you’re down in the dumps seeing that and moments later the whole dugout erupts,” Tracy said. “We haven’t been doing much offensively for a few days and to get a swing right there and feel like you steal a game, it was enormous. Big emotion swing.”
With the lead in hand, Wyatt Olds and Alec Gamboa pitched a scoreless eighth, and with Aroldis Chapman unavailable, Garrett Whitlock came on for the ninth and locked down the save for the win. Story and Sogard turned inning-ending double plays in both the eighth and the ninth to ensure the Rangers couldn’t mount one last comeback.
“Good teams find a way to win and we’ve been doing that in the second half and that’s kind of who you become,” Story said. “And you feel that momentum, you feel that vibe around the game and we never give up.”
X-rays negative, Chapman day-to-day
The Red Sox got some good news postgame when X-rays on Contreras’ hand came back negative.
“He’s got a bruise on the hand and some swelling,” Tracy said. “So we’ll just take it day to day and see how he is.”
Tracy also confirmed that Chapman has been dealing with some lat tightness for the past few days and they are taking a conservative approach.
“It’s getting better but have to make sure it gets there, that’s why he wasn’t available tonight,” Tracy said, adding that an IL stint isn’t being considered for Chapman right now.

item.title: [Boston Herald] Red Sox slugger leaves game after being hit by pitch in hand

Red Sox interim manager Chad Tracy told reporters in Texas following the club’s 4-3 win that X-rays on Contreras’ right hand came back negative and that he’ll be day to day going forward. “We did an X-ray, it’s negative, he’s got a bruise on the hand and some swelling,” Tracy said. “We’ll take it day to da
item.content:encoded:
The Red Sox held their breath after seeing one of their best hitters exit Thursday’s game after being hit in the hand by a pitch, but the initial reports on Willson Contreras were encouraging.
Red Sox interim manager Chad Tracy told reporters in Texas following the club’s 4-3 win that X-rays on Contreras’ right hand came back negative and that he’ll be day to day going forward.
“We did an X-ray, it’s negative, he’s got a bruise on the hand and some swelling,” Tracy said. “We’ll take it day to day and see how he is.”
Contreras left Thursday’s game after being hit in the right hand by a pitch in the top of the eighth inning. He immediately doubled over in pain and after a brief visit from the trainer walked straight to the dugout. He continued to grimace as he flexed his hand on the bench before departing into the tunnel for further testing.
Isiah Kiner-Falefa took Contreras’ place at first base.
With less than two weeks to play before the postseason the Red Sox cannot afford to be without Contreras. The veteran first baseman has been the club’s best hitter this season, leading the team with 27 home runs to go along with a .276 average and a .905 OPS.
The dour mood quickly turned to elation after Trevor Story put the Red Sox ahead with a three-run home run moments after Contreras was hit. With the win the Red Sox’s magic number is now three with nine games to play, giving the club some badly needed breathing room and potentially the luxury of giving Contreras extra rest if further imaging doesn’t reveal anything worse than a bruise.

item.content:encoded:
The Red Sox could get an important arm back in the fold sometime soon.
Right-hander Johan Oviedo, whom Boston acquired in a five-player offseason trade with the Pirates, made a rehab appearance on Thursday with Triple-A Worcester. He gave up one earned run in 2 1/3 innings against the Rays’ Durham affiliate, allowing two hits and a walk and striking out four.
It was Oviedo’s first rehab appearance since he was placed on the injured list back on April 3, retroactive to March 31, with a right flexor strain. Oviedo was transferred to the 60-day IL on April 14, but Thursday’s outing is a sign he might not be lost for the season. Primarily a starter, Oviedo threw just 30 pitches for Worcester and will likely need multiple additional outings to build up and shake off any rust.
The right-hander made just one appearance for the Red Sox before landing on the IL, allowing four runs on six hits in 3 2/3 relief innings on March 30 against the Astros in Houston. With the Pirates, Oviedo missed all of 2024 after undergoing Tommy John surgery but returned to make nine starts with a 3.57 ERA in 2025.
Boston's rotation is in solid shape even with Garrett Crochet (left shoulder inflammation) missing most of the year, but Oviedo -- if he can return in time -- could make an impact as a multi-inning reliever down the stretch or in the postseason.

Cotillo notes that Gray has touched on the potential of retirement in recent interviews and adds that the Red Sox do not believe that Gray is making an empty threat. However, Cotillo does add that some in the industry believe that Gray’s strong 2026 campaign could put him
item.content:encoded:
Instead of securing the bag this offseason, Sonny Gray might potentially be walking away from the bag.
The Boston Red Sox pitcher Gray could possibly retire after this season, Chris Cotillo of MassLive.com reported on Thursday. Cotillo notes that Gray has touched on the potential of retirement in recent interviews and adds that the Red Sox do not believe that Gray is making an empty threat.
However, Cotillo does add that some in the industry believe that Gray’s strong 2026 campaign could put him in a position to receive a new contract in the range of three years and $75 million (if Gray decides to keep pitching). You can read Cotillo’s full report on the situation here.
Gray is 36 years old now but is still very much at the top of his game. A three-time MLB All-Star, Gray has enjoyed a big-time resurgence this season, leading Major League Baseball with 17 wins to go along with a 2.76 ERA and a 1.17 WHIP through 27 starts.
As it stands right now, Gray has a $30 million mutual option with the Red Sox for the 2027 campaign. But with a $10 million buyout clause, Gray can easily decide to opt out and test free agency.
Gray is a 14-year veteran in an MLB landscape where pitchers can sometimes last into their early 40s. The right-hander also drew trade interest from some prominent teams at this year’s deadline, but he may stunningly be considering the possibility of walking away after the season.

item.title: [The Boston Globe] Pinkie injury may be affecting Caleb Durbin, but it’s not keeping him out of Red Sox lineup - The Boston Globe
item.dc:creator: Alex Speier
item.description: ARLINGTON, Texas — Nearly three months after Caleb Durbin first dislocated his left pinkie and more than a month after he reinjured it, the third baseman’s digit remains locked nearly at a right angle. “It doesn’t quite straighten or bend all the way,” Durbin acknowledged. item.content:encoded:
ARLINGTON, Texas — Nearly three months after Caleb Durbin first dislocated his left pinkie and more than a month after he reinjured it, the third baseman’s digit remains locked nearly at a right angle.
“It doesn’t quite straighten or bend all the way,” Durbin acknowledged.
Durbin received X-rays after his initial injury against the Rockies on June 24 and the reinjury against the White Sox on Aug. 6. In both instances, there was no fracture and he was told playing was simply a matter of pain tolerance.
And so, there was little question about how he’d proceed. He didn’t seek more information.
“There really is kind of a joint understanding [with the team] that we’ll get it looked at at the end of the season if we have to, because [whatever the diagnosis is], it’s not going to impact my decision to play at all,” he said.
Still, Durbin recognizes fingers shouldn’t look like they could be used to mount a shelf. Might he require offseason surgery?
“I don’t know yet. We’ll find out,” he said. “I hope there’s something we can do about it. But we’ll get there when the time comes.”
For now, Durbin remains a lineup constant. Thursday’s contest against the Rangers marked his 145th game of the season. He continues to deliver Gold Glove-caliber defense (his six outs above average lead AL third basemen) while also pushing the envelope on the field with high-IQ plays, most recently advancing from first to third on an infield single on Wednesday.
“He plays the game that way,” said Sox interim manager Chad Tracy. “It’s what he does.”
Still, it seems the injury is impacting him at the plate. He’s hitting .211/.400/.316 in September — showing fight in his at-bats (thus his standout on-base percentage), but rarely driving the ball. His whiff rate (10 percent of swings) is the lowest for any month this year, but he’s rarely been able to drive the ball. His 48 percent ground ball rate is his highest in any month since May.
But to Durbin, the question of whether or how the injury might be affecting him is secondary. His primary concern is simply whether he is positioned to contribute in any way.
“The pain’s gone down drastically since it happened the second time,” Durbin shrugged. “It’s functional.”
Updates on injured trio
Garrett Crochet, who last threw off a mound on Tuesday, worked out at Polar Park in Worcester on Thursday and will continue to throw on flat ground on Friday before the team decides whether to introduce any higher-intensity activities over the weekend.
Tracy said there’s been no discussion about the lefthander pitching in a rehab game for the WooSox this weekend. He didn’t rule out the possibility Crochet could soon face hitters in a live batting practice session, but made clear that there is no known schedule involving the 27-year-old.
“It all depends on how he’s feeling. … He’s been down so long,” said Tracy. “It is day to day. [Friday he’ll] throw, see how he feels, and then determine what the weekend holds.”
Righthander Tyron Guerrero, whose return from shoulder inflammation was delayed slightly by lower back cramps, had a high-intensity throwing session on flat ground. He’s expected to throw off a mound Friday when the Sox open a three-game series at Tampa Bay, a potential prelude to activation later in the weekend. “The shoulder feels great, the arm feels great,” said Guerrero.
Ceddanne Rafaela is increasing (right quad strain) is increasing his agility work but, at this point, there’s “no discernible timeline yet on game action,” according to Tracy. It hasn’t been determined if Rafaela will join the Sox in Tampa.
Oviedo in Worcester
Righthander Johan Oviedo (right elbow strain), pitching in an official game for the first time since March 30, struck out four batters while sitting at 96 miles per hour and touching 99 with his four-seamer in 2⅓ innings in a rehab appearance for the WooSox. He threw 20 of 30 pitches for strikes … Ranger Suarez will start for the Sox on Friday against the Rays, but the Sox have yet to decide who will start the other two games of the series. Payton Tolle, Patrick Sandoval, and Brayan Bello are all considerations … The Red Sox will send two scouts to New York for next week’s four-game Yankees-Rays series, the start of the team’s in-person advance scouting efforts for the postseason.
Alex Speier can be reached at alex.speier@globe.com. Follow him @alexspeier.

item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox starter is working his way back from a right elbow injury.
Video Transcript
What's up, everyone?
Zach Coe here for Roundtable.
Ahead of Tuesday night's loss to the Rangers, Red Sox interim manager Chad Tracy told reporters that reliever Justin Slayton's season was over after an orthopedic visit revealed degenerative changes in his flexor mass, which required a PRP injection, effectively ending his season.
So obviously, the Red Sox have one of the best bullpens in baseball, backend of Aroldis Chapman, Justin Slayton, and Tayron Guerrero when he returns from the injured list.
But the loss of Slayton is still a really big one for this Red Sox bullpen, especially in the postseason when managers tend to be more aggressive with the hooks on both starters and relievers.
It was a pretty underwhelming season for Slayton when you look at the final line.
It was a 4.60 ERA in 31 1/3 innings.
But he was prone to a couple blowup starts, and that really inflated his ERA for much of the season.
It'll be interesting to see how Tracy's able to piece together the bullpen in Slayton's absence.
Of course, like I said, you have the backend pretty solidified with Tayron Guerrero handling the seventh, Garrett Whitlock in the eighth to All-Star Aroldis Chapman, who's been one of the best closers in baseball over the last two seasons.
But it's how you get to them that I really have some concerns about, and there are plenty of guys that are available to fill that role, but it's whether or not they'll be able to capitalize on their opportunities.
First one being Greg Weiser.
I wrote about it a little bit earlier, but ever since he was recalled from his brief demotion to Triple-A, he's been incredible for the Red Sox, stepping up as they lost guys like Whitlock to an IL stint, Slayton, who landed on the IL shortly after Whitlock, and most recently Guerrero.
There's also Tanner Houk, who's working his way back from Tommy John surgery he underwent last year.
He's gonna try to make a return in a bullpen capacity for the last week of the season.
And then there's the big wild card of it all in Garrett Crochet, who continues to throw side sessions as he tries to get back in a relief role for the postseason.
He's been on the injured list since April 29th with left shoulder inflammation.
So any of those guys are more than capable of stepping up and filling that role.
It's just gonna be about whether or not they're, one, healthy enough to go out there and throw on a near nightly basis like the team might need them to in the postseason, and two, whether or not they're gonna be productive enough.
Obviously, with Houk, he's coming back from Tommy John surgery, and typically you see guys be a little bit wild with their control when they first come back from Tommy John.
We saw it in Houk's first relea-- We saw it in his first rehab appearance with Portland.
He walked two guys, and a run scored as a result.
But it's been a little bit better, since then in the two appearances following that.
So we'll see if that is something that he can shake.
And then Crochet, he's just We haven't seen him in so long, it's tough to say whether or not he's gonna be as effective as he once was.
And even if he isn't able to get to the 2025 Cy Young runner-up caliber, can he at least give you enough to kind of bridge that gap between the starter and to the backend of your bullpen?
And then there's kind of a wild card in it all, and a bit of a forgotten man in Johan Oviedo, who obviously has electric stuff, but he's made only one appearance in a Red Sox uniform before landing on the IL with right elbow inflammation.
So he's planning on making a rehab appearance with Triple-A Worcester on Thursday night, and then they'll figure out the next steps with him.
But Red Sox have plenty of options to fill that void left behind by Slayton.

item.content:encoded:
New Red Sox Rumors on Sonny Gray's Potential MLB FA Contract Amid Retirement Speculation
Sonny Gray is enjoying one of the best seasons of his career at 36 years old, and it could lead to a big payday in free agency — if he continues playing beyond the 2026 campaign.
According to Mass Live's Chris Cotillo, the Boston Red Sox's ace could command a deal similar to the three-year, $75 million deal the Texas Rangers gave Nathan Eovaldi two years ago.
But Gray isn't fully set on returning to baseball.
Cotillo noted that Gray said in an interview with The Boston Globe recently that he would retire "in a heartbeat" if his family gave any indication that they wanted him to be home year-round.
Cotillo added that those within the organization take Gray's talks of retirement seriously. He has spent off days this season visiting his family's home in Nashville, regardless of where the team is playing.
"We can get into that at another time but not right now," Gray said when asked about retirement, per Cotillo.
Whether Gray will call it quits after this year remains to be seen, but he'll look to finish off his renaissance season strong. He's tied for the best record in baseball at 17-5, notching a 2.76 ERA and 1.17 WHIP with 140 strikeouts.
With Gray's help, the Red Sox turned their season around and are now on the precipice of securing the second wild-card spot at 82-70.

item.title: [Boston Herald] Injured Red Sox right-hander takes mound for first time since March

item.content:encoded:
Originally viewed as one of the favorites to start the season in the Opening Day rotation, Red Sox right-hander Johan Oviedo wound up making just one appearance out of the bullpen before going on the shelf with a right elbow strain.
Now after missing nearly the entire season, Oviedo may finally be nearing a return.
Oviedo began a rehab assignment at Triple-A Worcester on Thursday, throwing 2 1/3 innings for the WooSox in his first game action since late March.
The 28-year-old threw 30 pitches, 20 for strikes, while allowing one run on two hits and a walk while striking out four. Oviedo allowed an RBI double with one out in the top of the second before striking out the final three batters he faced.
More encouragingly, Oviedo’s fastball averaged 95.9 mph and topped out at 98.5, a sizable jump from the 92-93 he averaged earlier in the season.
Originally acquired last winter from the Pittsburgh Pirates as part of the Jhostynxon Garcia trade, Oviedo was initially expected to provide rotation depth as a possible high-ceiling power arm. Oviedo had previously missed extensive time due to Tommy John surgery, but finished his last season in Pittsburgh strong with a 3.57 ERA and 42 strikeouts over nine starts down the stretch.
The righty entered spring as one of the favorites for the No. 5 rotation spot, but after some promising early starts began showing signs of wear. The last rotation spot wound up going to Connelly Early, with Oviedo making the team as a reliever, and he made one appearance against the Houston Astros on March 30, allowing four runs over 3 2/3 innings.
Oviedo has been on the injured list ever since, but now he could be a dark horse candidate for the Red Sox playoff roster along with Tanner Houck and Garrett Crochet, who are also working their way back from extended injury absences.
Upcoming starters
Ranger Suarez will start Friday’s series opener against the Tampa Bay Rays, but the Red Sox’s other starters remain to be determined. Payton Tolle would normally be in line to start Saturday but Red Sox interim manager Chad Tracy told reporters in Texas on Thursday that the club is still deciding how it wants to handle the weekend.
Brayan Bello, who was limited to 19 pitches over 1 2/3 innings on Tuesday, would presumably be a candidate to start one of this weekend’s games.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Sonny Gray's Rumored Price Tag Shouldn't Scare Red Sox Off
item.dc:creator: Patrick McAvoy; Unknown
item.description: The Boston Red Sox made one of the very best moves in baseball for the 2026 season, despite the fact that some fans didn't initially believe in the deal. item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox made one of the very best moves in baseball for the 2026 season, despite the fact that some fans didn't initially believe in the deal.
While searching for a No. 2 starter last offseason, Boston turned to the St. Louis Cardinals and swung a deal for three-time All-Star Sonny Gray. With the Red Sox searching for another elite starter, some wondered if Gray was better suited for a mid-to-back of the rotation spot, rather than the No. 2 spot for a club with World Series aspirations. He has more than delivered and has been Boston's best starter all season. Gray's going to get Cy Young Award votes and Boston should do what it can to try to keep him in town beyond the 2026 season. If he plays, he'll cost a pretty penny. MassLive.com's Chris Cotillo reported that some in the industry believe Gray will get a deal in the range of three years and $75 million — or more — if he continues his career.
"As a free agent, Gray’s renaissance season may position him to receive a lucrative deal that some in the industry expect to match or exceed the three-year, $75 million deal the Rangers gave to Nathan Eovaldi two winters ago," Cotillo wrote. "Interestingly, though, Gray has not committed to pitching again in 2027. In a recent interview with The Boston Globe, Gray said he would retire 'in a heartbeat' if his family signaled that he was wanted back home year-round, even if that meant retiring after the end of this year."
The Red Sox Should Do Everything To Keep Sonny Gray
That's actually also the same deal that the Cardinals gave Gray before the 2024 season as well. He inked a three-year, $75 million pact that he's currently in the final year of. After the season, Gray has a $30 million mutual option for the 2027 season with a $10 million buyout. If Boston picks up its end of the buyout and Gray opts out, then the buyout would be forfeited.
Gray has pitched well enough in a Red Sox uniform to get paid again — if he keeps pitching. So far this season, he has a 17-5 record, 2.76 ERA and 4.0 wins above replacement in 156 2/3 innings pitched. When it comes to Gray, his age stands out at 36 years old. But it hasn't stopped him yet. The price of pitching has gone up in a big way. A deal with a $25 million annual value, as Cotillo pointed out, would be in the range of guys like Michael King, Sean Manaea, and Eovaldi. It would be just above guys like Aaron Nola, Seth Lugo, Robbie Ray and Luis Severino. Gray has been better than all of these guys so far this season.
When it comes to the Red Sox, there isn't as much pitching depth down in the minors as there once was. Over the last year, Boston has traded guys like Hunter Dobbins, Richard Fitts, Brandon Clarke, Anthony Eyanson and Kyson Witherspoon, among others. Plus, Connelly Early was traded as well.
Garrett Crochet, Payton Tolle, Ranger Suárez, and Jake Bennett are locks for the 2027 rotation. Johan Oviedo is someone who could play a role. Tanner Houck is another guy who could as well. We've seen all season how impactful injuries are to the rotation. You never have enough arms. A dependable veteran like Gray for the next few years should be a necessity. It's no guarantee that he pitches beyond the 2026 season, but if he does, it should be in a Boston uniform.
Patrick McAvoy's experiences include local and national sports coverage at the New England Sports Network with a focus on baseball and basketball. Outside of journalism, Patrick received an MBA at Brandeis University. For all business/marketing inquiries regarding Boston Red Sox On SI, please reach out to Scott Neville: scott@moreviewsmedia.com
Follow patmcavoy

item.title: [BoSox Injection] Red Sox fans may have spoken too soon on winner of Caleb Durbin-Kyle Harrison trade
item.dc:creator: Brandon Glick
item.description: We won't spend too long belaboring how bad the Kyle Harrison-Caleb Durbin looked for the Boston Red Sox after a few months; the southpaw had emerged as a genuine National League Cy Young contender for the Milwaukee Brewers in the first half, while the third baseman was one of the league's worst qualified hitters through the beginning of June. item.content:encoded:
We won't spend too long belaboring how bad the Kyle Harrison-Caleb Durbin looked for the Boston Red Sox after a few months; the southpaw had emerged as a genuine National League Cy Young contender for the Milwaukee Brewers in the first half, while the third baseman was one of the league's worst qualified hitters through the beginning of June. Tack on the fact that Shane Drohan has become a valuable starter in his own right this year while Andruw Monasterio has been worth negative fWAR, and you've got a recipe for an all-time disaster of a trade.
And yet, after the tide began shifting over the summer, we can now definitively say the pendulum has swung back in the other direction. Durbin has been a star since June 1, posting an .812 OPS and a 129 wRC+. Meanwhile, Harrison is struggling so badly that he's now been moved out of the Brewers' rotation entirely.
It's far too early to suggest that the Red Sox have made up that early gap and are now the winners of the blockbuster trade, but it's clear that their decision to go all-in for Durbin wasn't a foolish one.
Red Sox just need to break even now to win Caleb Durbin trade in the future
In that same post-June-1 span, Harrison has pitched to an 6.10 ERA and 5.38 FIP, allowing a whopping 17 home runs over just 59 innings. A bout with forearm tightness near the All-Star break definitely has something to do with his second-half collapse, but he hasn't been pitching like an ace for quite a while. The fact that there's been conversations about him being left off the Brewers' postseason roster entirely should tell you all you need to know about the southpaw's recent struggles.
Durbin is trending in the exact opposite direction, as he's currently the seventh-most valuable third baseman in the league by fWAR (2.9) this season. A lot of that has to do with how excellent his baserunning and glove have been, but saying that someone is above average in every phase of the game isn't exactly a bad thing. He's a couple of steals and some favorable votes away from a 20 SB, Gold Glove campaign in his Red Sox debut. Not too shabby, eh?
It's also worth factoring in the other players Craig Breslow pried out of Milwaukee; neither Monasterio nor Anthony Seigler have been great in limited duty in Boston, but the former has produced some timely hits while playing all four infield positions while the latter has a 102 wRC+ in just under 175 plate appearances this year.
Then there's Owen Hull, whom the Red Sox selected with the compensatory draft pick the Brewers forked over in the trade. All he did after being drafted was mash in High-A, posting a .967 OPS in 24 games.
With Durbin under contract through 2031 and Hull sure to fly up the prospect rankings over the offseason, there's a good chance that the Sox can win this trade down the road, so long as they continue to break even for now.

item.content:encoded:
The Red Sox magic number has been stubbornly stuck at five for the last couple of days, and while there's no real concern about them ultimately getting in, it would be nice to win tonight and knock that down to three (Red Sox win + Rangers loss).
Another reason it would be nice to win this game is because Sonny Gray is starting, and this is his second to last start before the postseason. Ideally, he'll be locking in for an excellent outing at the end of the month. Despite the loss last time out against the Royals, he still boasts a 17-5 person record, which is 12 games over .500, and also the exact number of games the team is over .500 at 82-70. (Make of that what you will.)
Lineup wise, Nick Sogard is back at second base after Isiah Kiner-Falefa got a start there last night. Also, with Texas throwing lefty Cody Bradford, Jahmai Jones is at DH instead of Mickey Gasper. As usual, we'll probably see a pinch hit to switch the platoon advantage there at some point in the game.

item.content:encoded:
ARLINGTON, Texas (AP) — Willson Contreras left the Boston's 4-3 win over Texas on Thursday night in the eighth inning after he was hit by a pitch on his right hand.
Red Sox manager Chad Tracy said the first baseman's hand was bruised with some swelling and X-rays were negative.
“We're going to take it day to day,” Tracy said.
Contreras was struck by a first-pitch sinker from Jakob Junis after Wilyer Abreu drew a leadoff walk with the Rangers leading 3-1. Contreras walked to first base in obvious pain, was examined by an athletic trainer and headed to the dugout.
Two batters later, Trevor Story hit a three-run home run off Jacob Latz.
Contreras was 1 for 3 with a single. He was hit by a pitch Wednesday night after hitting a two-run home run in the first inning of Boston's 7-3 loss to the Rangers.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] How Will Boston Red Sox Bullpen Replace Justin Slaten in Postseason?
item.dc:creator: Zach Coe
item.description: RedSoxRoundtable's Zach Coe discusses the potential relievers who could step up and fill the void left behind by Justin Slaten after it was revealed the right-hander was unlikely to return from the injured list in 2026. Be sure to join our FREE community over on RedSoxRoundtable.com! item.content:encoded:
RedSoxRoundtable's Zach Coe discusses the potential relievers who could step up and fill the void left behind by Justin Slaten after it was revealed the right-hander was unlikely to return from the injured list in 2026. Be sure to join our FREE community over on RedSoxRoundtable.com!
After an incredible July that saw the Boston Red Sox go 21-4, ultimately saving their season and propelling them into postseason position, the team has given key contributors time on the injured list to address lingering injuries. Among the players placed on the IL was right-handed reliever Justin Slaten, who was dealing with right elbow soreness.
After initially expecting to miss the minimum of 15 days or somewhere close to it, the 29-year-old continued to experience soreness as he began throwing progressions, leading the team to shut him down each time. On Tuesday, interim manager Chad Tracy announced that Slaten received a PRP injection to treat "degenerative changes in his flexor mass," ending his season.
With Slaten set to miss the remainder of the year, the pressure is on these pitchers to help bridge the gap between the starter and All-Star closer Aroldis Chapman:
Tyron Guerrero
Guerrero was expected to be activated off the injured list ahead of Wednesday night's loss to the Texas Rangers, but tightness in his lower back led the team to delay his activation. Still, though, upon his activation, Guerrero will become one of the primary seventh-inning options for Tracy to turn to.
The 35-year-old flamethrower has been an incredible find for Chief Baseball Officer Craig Breslow, posting a 3.26 ERA in 38.2 innings in 2026. However, he hit a rough patch before landing on the IL, allowing eight earned runs in his last 13.2 innings. Boston will need him to return to the pitcher he was for the first 38.2 innings of his season, when he posted a 2.16 ERA.
After not allowing a single earned run in his first 10 appearances after being dealt to Boston at the trade deadline, the 28-year-old lefty has struggled in his last six outings, allowing five earned runs, including three in a blow-up appearance in Wednesday's loss.
Miller told reporters after the loss that he was working through a mechanical issue that led to the struggles. However, he is the primary left-handed high-leverage arm before Chapman, so the team will need him to get those issues squared away ahead of what's likely to be a Wild Card-round matchup against a New York Yankees lineup that's lefty-heavy.
No single pitcher has stepped up more for the Red Sox as they shuffled Garrett Whitlock, Slaten, and Guerrero on the injured list than Weissert. After a brief demotion to Triple-A Worcester on Aug. 7, Weissert returned to the big leagues on Aug. 13, taking Whitlock's spot on the active roster, and has been lights out ever since. In 10.2 innings since being recalled, the 31-year-old right-hander has allowed only two earned runs on 12 hits, striking out 14 and walking only four.
Weissert figures to be the leader in the clubhouse to take over Slaten's role in the bullpen.
A trio of injured options
The Red Sox have several pitchers looking to return from the injured list before the end of the regular season who could factor into the team's playoff push, including 2025 Cy Young Award runner-up Garrett Crochet, 2024 All-Star Tanner Houck, and Johan Oviedo.
Crochet
The 27-year-old ace has thrown four bullpen sessions since restarting a throwing progression on Aug. 3, with his most recent outing, a 30-pitch up-and-down session on the Fenway Park mound, coming on Tuesday afternoon. While Crochet, if healthy enough to appear in games, will almost certainly be on the postseason roster, he is expected to make multi-inning appearances rather than one-inning spurts like Slaten had been used, making him a valuable weapon but an imperfect replacement.
Houck
The now-30-year-old right-hander is attempting to return to the Boston staff in a "Swiss Army knife" role after undergoing Tommy John surgery in August 2025. Houck has already made three rehab appearances with both Double-A Portland and Triple-A Worcester, allowing two earned runs on one hit, walking four, and striking out seven in 4.2 innings. He is expected to return to Worcester on Saturday for a 40-50 pitch outing before potentially rejoining the Red Sox.
Though what exactly Houck can contribute after being out of major league action since May 2025 remains to be seen.
Oviedo
A bit of a forgotten man in the 2026 Red Sox season is the 28-year-old right-hander, who made only one appearance before landing on the injured list on April 3 with right elbow inflammation. Oviedo will make his first rehab appearance Thursday night with Worcester before deciding on next steps; at this point, the risk likely outweighs the reward of making the postseason roster.
Tracy, Breslow, and the rest of Boston's decision makers will have 10 games to make their final decisions on how exactly the postseason roster will look, and who will replace Slaten's high-leverage innings.
Up next for the Sox
The Red Sox will look to avoid the sweep at the hands of the Texas Rangers in Thursday's series finale from Globe Life Field. Sonny Gray (17-5, 2.76 ERA) gets the start for Boston opposite Tyler Alexander (5-2, 3.38 ERA) for Texas. First pitch is set for 8:05 p.m. ET.

item.title: [NESN] Red Sox Make Notable Lineup Change For Crucial Rangers Finale | NESN
item.dc:creator: Rodney Knuppel
item.description: The Boston Red Sox need something to change Thursday night. Putting Jarren Duran back in the lineup is a start. Boston will turn to Duran in center field for Thursday's series finale against the Texas Rangers at Globe Life Field after he did not start Wednesday's 7-3 loss. The Red Sox have dropped the first two games of the series and enter Thursday at 82-70 with only 10 games remaining in the regular season. item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox need something to change Thursday night. Putting Jarren Duran back in the lineup is a start.
Boston will turn to Duran in center field for Thursday's series finale against the Texas Rangers at Globe Life Field after he did not start Wednesday's 7-3 loss. The Red Sox have dropped the first two games of the series and enter Thursday at 82-70 with only 10 games remaining in the regular season.
Roman Anthony will remain in the leadoff spot and start in left field, while Jahmai Jones gets another opportunity at designated hitter. Wilyer Abreu, Willson Contreras and Adley Rutschman make up the middle of the order.
Christopher Smith of MassLive shared Boston's lineup shortly after it was released Thursday.
The complete Red Sox lineup:
- Roman Anthony, LF
- Jahmai Jones, DH
- Wilyer Abreu, RF
- Willson Contreras, 1B
- Adley Rutschman, C
- Trevor Story, SS
- Jarren Duran, CF
- Caleb Durbin, 3B
- Nick Sogard, 2B
Sonny Gray will start on the mound.
Red Sox bring Duran back for crucial series finale
Duran's return is one of the most notable changes from Wednesday's lineup. The 30-year-old was not in the starting nine Wednesday, when Boston used Nate Eaton in center field and Isiah Kiner-Falefa at second base.
Red Sox lineup: Anthony LF, Jones DH, Abreu RF, Contreras 1B, Rutschman C, Story SS, Duran LF, Durbin 3B, Sogard 2B, Gray P
— Christopher Smith (@SmittyOnMLB) September 17, 2026
Neither is starting Thursday.
Instead, Duran returns to center, Sogard takes over at second and Trevor Story moves up one spot in the order to hit sixth.
Boston could certainly use a spark.
The Red Sox entered Texas with an opportunity to strengthen their postseason position but instead have lost consecutive games to a Rangers team fighting for its own playoff life. Texas improved to 76-76 with Wednesday's victory and has won four consecutive games. The Rangers are only one game behind the Chicago White Sox for the final American League wild-card spot.
Boston remains in much better shape, holding the second AL wild card with a five-game cushion over Chicago entering Thursday. That cushion is significant. It isn't comfortable enough to keep losing.
The Red Sox have gone 5-5 over their last 10 games, and Thursday represents their final opportunity to leave Texas with something positive before the schedule moves into its final nine games.
Sonny Gray gets the ball with Red Sox needing a win
If there is a pitcher Boston would want on the mound in this situation, Gray makes a compelling case. The veteran right-hander enters Thursday with a 17-5 record and 2.76 ERA.
Texas will counter with left-hander Tyler Alexander, who enters at 5-2 with a 3.38 ERA. The left-handed starter helps explain some of Boston's lineup decisions.
Jones, a right-handed hitter, remains in the No. 2 spot after starting there Wednesday. Contreras gives Boston another right-handed bat in the cleanup position, while Rutschman follows him from the fifth spot.
Anthony remains atop everything.
Boston has continued trusting the rookie in the leadoff role during the most important stretch of the season, and that won't change with a left-hander on the mound Thursday.
The larger question is whether the Red Sox can finally turn opportunities into enough runs.
Boston's postseason position remains favorable, but the Rangers have provided a reminder of how quickly September can become uncomfortable.
A sweep would send the Red Sox into the final nine games on a three-game losing streak. A win would allow them to leave Texas with their playoff cushion intact and Gray having stopped the bleeding. With Duran back in the lineup, Boston is hoping Thursday looks considerably different from the first two nights of the series. First pitch from Globe Life Field is scheduled for 8:05 p.m. ET.

item.title: [NBC Sports Boston] Five biggest issues plaguing Red Sox with postseason looming
item.dc:creator: Justin Leger
item.description: The Boston Red Sox are still sitting comfortably in the second Wild Card spot, but there are several issues they must resolve before they start thinking about playoff baseball. Boston is a mediocre 11-11 over its last 22 games. While that's been good enough to sustain its playoff position, its play hasn't exactly inspired optimism for a deep postseason run. Most of the Red Sox' problems can be linked to their underperforming lineup. Key hitters like Roman Anthony, Willson Contreras, Adley Rutsch
item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox are still sitting comfortably in the second Wild Card spot, but there are several issues they must resolve before they start thinking about playoff baseball.
Boston is a mediocre 11-11 over its last 22 games. While that's been good enough to sustain its playoff position, its play hasn't exactly inspired optimism for a deep postseason run.
Most of the Red Sox' problems can be linked to their underperforming lineup. Key hitters like Roman Anthony, Willson Contreras, Adley Rutschman and Wilyer Abreu have been concerningly inconsistent.
A deeper dive into the numbers suggests the struggling Sox will have their work cut out for them in their presumed Wild Card Series rematch at Yankee Stadium. Here are the club's five biggest areas of concern with 10 games remaining:
Roman Anthony is ice-cold
The Red Sox need Roman Anthony to be one of their best offensive players to have any chance of a deep postseason run. If the former No. 1 prospect continues to play the way he has for most of September, that will be problematic.
Anthony is hitting just .149 (7-for-47) with one home run and a .428 OPS over his last 11 games. He has struck out 18 times in 51 plate appearances.
The 22-year-old's struggles beg the question: should he still be the leadoff hitter in the postseason? Interim manager Chad Tracy will have no choice but to reevaluate Anthony's spot in the lineup if his woes continue. The problem with that is there aren't any exciting alternatives. The leadoff spot has been a glaring issue all season long, regardless of who has been thrust into the role.
Struggling against high velocity
The Red Sox offense has been inconsistent no matter who's on the mound, but it has mostly struggled against pitchers with high velo. Here's how some of Boston's regulars have fared this season against pitches greater than or equal to 97 mph:
- Wilyer Abreu: .170 BA, .623 OPS (237 pitches)
- Jarren Duran: .065 BA, .300 OPS (203 pitches)
- Willson Contreras: .170 BA, .512 OPS (166 pitches)
- Ceddanne Rafaela: .205 BA, .449 OPS (157 pitches)
- Roman Anthony: .091 BA, .440 OPS (58 pitches)
- Adley Rutschman: .077 BA, .451 OPS (57 pitches)
The Red Sox' top performer against high velocity (97 mph and above) has been Caleb Durbin (.364 BA, .912 OPS, 161 pitches).
Being so vulnerable against high velocity will especially be a problem for Boston in its expected Wild Card Series matchup against the New York Yankees. Cy Young frontrunner and likely Game 1 starter Cam Schlittler averages 98 mph with his four-seam fastball, which he uses 44.5 percent of the time. Gerrit Cole averages 96.9 mph with his four-seam, using it 49.3 percent of the time.
Leaving runners stranded
Boston has been below average all season at capitalizing on runners in scoring position. It currently ranks 17th in batting average (.250) and 21st in OPS (.731) with RISP. They're hitting just .212 in such situations through 14 games so far in September.
The Yankees' elite pitching staff probably won't provide the Red Sox with many scoring opportunities in their short series, so it's imperative that they come through when given the chance. Lately, Boston hasn't had anyone in its lineup to feel confident about when they step to the plate with runners on.
Role players regressing
As great as guys like Willson Contreras, Caleb Durbin, and Wilyer Abreu were throughout the Red Sox' incredible midseason turnaround, it was the role players who powered their surge. Mickey Gasper, Jahmai Jones, Nick Sogard, Anthony Seigler, and Andruw Monasterio were instrumental in resurrecting Boston's season.
Gasper has cooled off, though no one expected him to sustain his Barry Bonds-like run. Jahmai Jones is 4 for his last 22 (.182) with nine strikeouts, suddenly making him a playoff roster cut candidate. Sogard is still hitting, but his .758 OPS so far in September suggests regression to the mean. Seigler is hurt. Monasterio posted a .578 OPS in August and is 0-for-11 so far in September, putting him on the playoff roster bubble.
That group deserves immense credit for getting the Red Sox here, but it cannot be counted on to propel the club through the postseason.
Erik Miller experiencing command issues
Boston's bullpen is arguably its biggest strength heading into the postseason. The back end with Garrett Whitlock, Tyron Guerrero, and Aroldis Chapman is elite.
We would've included trade deadline addition Erik Miller in that group last month, when he allowed only one earned run with 20 strikeouts and just three walks across his first 11 appearances with the Red Sox. His performance so far this month, however, has been alarming.
Miller, acquired from the San Francisco Giants in the Marcelo Mayer trade, has allowed four earned runs with six walks and six strikeouts through five appearances (4.1 IP) in September. His command struggles were a question mark upon his joining the club, and it appears that issue has reemerged with less than two weeks until the playoffs.
After Wednesday's poor outing against the Texas Rangers (2 H, 3 ER, 1 BB), Miller attributed his recent struggles to his mechanics. The Red Sox will hope that whatever the problem is, it's a quick fix, because Miller will be counted on to be their most reliable left-handed reliever not named Aroldis Chapman.

item.title: [Over the Monster] Red Sox News & Links: How concerning is Roman Anthony’s slump?

item.description: Garett Crochet wants to pitch in the postseason without making a single rehab appearance. That’s audacious enough, but how about playing in the postseason, without having ever played in the big leagues at all? That could be the situation Braiden Ward finds himself in. If you need to refresh your memory, Ward was the little speedster who was running wild all over Grapefruit League diamonds this spring. He hasn’t gotten a chance to show whether he can do that in the Majors yet, but Chad Tracy isn’
item.content:encoded:
Garett Crochet wants to pitch in the postseason without making a single rehab appearance. That’s audacious enough, but how about playing in the postseason, without having ever played in the big leagues at all? That could be the situation Braiden Ward finds himself in. If you need to refresh your memory, Ward was the little speedster who was running wild all over Grapefruit League diamonds this spring. He hasn’t gotten a chance to show whether he can do that in the Majors yet, but Chad Tracy isn’t ruling it out. “Every time he gets on, he’s not afraid,” Tracy said. “That’s the thing. If he gets on base, he’s looking to go. That’s a unique trait. There’s a lot of guys who can run and steal bases and then there’s other guys who are, every single time they get on, almost regardless of the timing.” (Conor Ryan, Boston.com)
But a lack of speed on the base paths isn’t really the Red Sox problem right now as they muddle through a middling September. Strikeouts are. “The Red Sox are swinging and missing too much and not walking enough. This month, they have the eighth-most strikeouts and seventh-fewest walks. That doesn’t play in the postseason. Making contact does.” (Rob Bradford, WEEI)
After he initially returned to the big leagues with a bang, Roman Anthony is one of the Sox hitters who’s struggling to make contact right now. But he doesn’t sound worried. “I’m right where I want to be,” said Anthony. “I came back with enough time to get a good number of plate appearances, and to fail like I am right now and to succeed like I did in the beginning, and then kind of meet in the middle and continue to grind out every single day and get ready for what we want to be a long postseason run. [The playoffs are] what you play for after such a long year … At the end of the day, those few weeks are the only thing that really matters.” (Alex Speier, Boston Globe)
Unfortunately, the other big power threat in the Sox lineup is also struggling to get back up to speed. Willson Contreras homered last night, but he’s still dealing with a nagging hamstring injury. “I ran pretty good there on the ground ball to shortstop, but I need to manage my leg better,” he said. “I know it’s feeling good and it’s feeling alright, but on a hard-hit ball like that, I know I’m going to be out. I was just trying to put pressure on him, see if he made a bad throw or whatever. Next time, I’ll manage better.” (Chris Cotillo, MassLive)
With Anthony and Contreras struggling in different ways, it’s important to remember that this team’s success has been built on depth, not individual star power. “Whether it was an expanded version of the trade that brought Caleb Durbin from Milwaukee to include Monasterio and Seigler, or waiver claims of Cheng and Gasper, or a minor league deal for Guerrero, the season has been a case study in the notion that perceived little moves can have a huge impact.” (Alex Speier, Boston Globe)
Fortunately, the Sox have some depth in the good guy department, too. After the departure of Liam Hendriks, who had been nominated for the Clemente Award seven times throughout his career for his charitable efforts, Garrett Whitlock has stepped in and picked up the baton. (Ian Browne, MLB.com)

item.title: [Fox News] Boston Red Sox send Sonny Gray to the mound against Texas Rangers in key MLB matchup tonight
item.dc:creator: David Troy
item.description: Yesterday was a winning day on the diamond as both MLB plays that I put out came through for us and cashed. We only have about 10 games remaining for the teams. The playoffs are within reach for some teams, and others are looking at some options for the future. Tonight we have a game between one team that has already locked up their spot, the Red Sox, and another team still battling to try and get in, the Rangers. The Boston Red Sox are 12 games above .500, and they have been one of the best tea
item.content:encoded:
Yesterday was a winning day on the diamond as both MLB plays that I put out came through for us and cashed. We only have about 10 games remaining for the teams. The playoffs are within reach for some teams, and others are looking at some options for the future. Tonight we have a game between one team that has already locked up their spot, the Red Sox, and another team still battling to try and get in, the Rangers.
The Boston Red Sox are 12 games above .500, and they have been one of the best teams in baseball over the past couple of months. They've been very streaky, winning multiple games at a time and moving up the standings. The Red Sox are currently sitting in the second spot in the Wild Card, and they control their own destiny. Much of the early-season problem was how the team was playing in Boston. They are just one game over .500 at home, but they are 11 games above on the road.
One guy who did excel in Fenway is tonight's starter, Sonny Gray. He has been good on the road as well and has put together one of the best seasons of his career. Gray is 17-5 with a 2.76 ERA and a 1.17 WHIP. This has been the most games he has ever won, and if it stands will be his second-lowest ERA ever. His road ERA is actually better than his home ERA, and his night games have been fantastic this season. He has thrown 13 innings this month and allowed just three earned runs. Gray faced the Rangers once this season, and he allowed just one earned run over six innings.
The Texas Rangers have a much more difficult path to the postseason. The team is .500 for the year, and there are questions about whether anyone who wins the American League West will finish the season with a winning record. They have chosen a great time to get hot, though, as they've won their past four games and are now tied with the Astros for the division lead. They are also just one game behind the White Sox for the final Wild Card spot. This game would go a long way for the team in getting closer to one of those two options.
Coming into the season, I was expecting the Rangers to be one of the better teams in the division, mostly due to their rotation. Jacob deGrom, Nathan Eovaldi, and MacKenzie Gore were guys I expected to give them a good chance in the majority of games. Tonight, though, the Rangers won't rely on their starters. They are sending out Tyler Alexander to start the game. He brings a 3.38 ERA and a 1.28 WHIP to the table over 66.2 innings. The Rangers have a rough bullpen with a collective 4.27 ERA.
I'm not really sure why the line is moving toward the Rangers for this game. Sonny Gray is a significantly better pitcher and way more reliable than anyone from the Rangers bullpen. The smart move, to me, is not to worry about the full game and just isolate when we can assume Gray will be on the hill. Give me the Red Sox through five innings.

item.title: [Fox News] Los Boston Red Sox sacan a Sonny Gray al montículo para enfrentarse a los Rangers de Texas , en un partido clave de la serie « MLB » esta noche
item.dc:creator: David
item.content:encoded:
{{#rendered}} {{/rendered}}
Ayer fue un día de victorias en el campo de béisbol, ya que las dos apuestas de « MLB » que publiqué nos dieron la razón y nos hicieron ganar. A los equipos solo les quedan unas 10 jornadas. Los playoffs están al alcance de algunos equipos, mientras que otros están barajando opciones de cara al futuro. Esta noche tenemos un partido entre un equipo que ya se ha asegurado su plaza, los Red Sox, y otro que sigue luchando por clasificarse, los Rangers.
Los Boston Red Sox están 12 partidos por encima del 50 %, y han sido uno de los mejores equipos de béisbol en los últimos meses. Han tenido rachas muy irregulares, ganando varios partidos seguidos y subiendo en la clasificación. Los Red Sox ocupan ahora mismo el segundo puesto en la clasificación de comodines y tienen el destino en sus manos. Gran parte del problema al principio de la temporada tenía que ver con cómo jugaba el equipo en Boston. En casa solo están un partido por encima del 50 %, pero fuera de casa están 11 partidos por encima.
Uno que sí ha destacado en Fenway es el lanzador titular de esta noche, Sonny Gray. También lo ha hecho bien fuera de casa y está cuajando una de las mejores temporadas de su carrera. Gray lleva un balance de 17-5, con una efectividad de 2,76 y un WHIP de 1,17. Es el mayor número de partidos que ha ganado nunca y, si se mantiene así, será la segunda efectividad más baja de su carrera. De hecho, su promedio de carreras limpias fuera de casa es mejor que el de casa, y sus partidos nocturnos han sido fantásticos esta temporada. Este mes ha lanzado 13 entradas y solo ha cedido tres carreras limpias. Gray se ha enfrentado a los Rangers una vez esta temporada y solo cedió una carrera limpia en seis entradas.
{{#rendered}} {{/rendered}}
Los Rangers deTexas tienen un camino mucho más difícil hacia la postemporada. El equipo tiene un balance de .500 en lo que va de año, y hay dudas sobre si el ganador de la División Oeste de la Liga Americana terminará la temporada con un balance positivo. Sin embargo, han elegido un momento genial para ponerse en racha, ya que han ganado sus últimos cuatro partidos y ahora están empatados con los Astros en el liderato de la división. Además, están a solo un partido de los White Sox por la última plaza de comodín. Este partido sería clave para que el equipo se acercara a una de esas dos opciones.
Al empezar la temporada, esperaba que los Rangers fueran uno de los mejores equipos de la división, sobre todo por su rotación de lanzadores. Jacob deGrom, Nathan Eovaldi y MacKenzie Gore eran los jugadores que, según yo, les darían muchas posibilidades en la mayoría de los partidos. Esta noche, sin embargo, los Rangers no van a confiar en sus titulares. Van a sacar a Tyler Alexander para abrir el partido. Llega con una ERA de 3,38 y un WHIP de 1,28 en 66,2 entradas. Los Rangers tienen un bullpen bastante flojo, con una ERA colectiva de 4,27.
{{#rendered}} {{/rendered}}
La verdad es que no tengo muy claro por qué la línea se está inclinando a favor de los Rangers en este partido. Sonny Gray es un lanzador mucho mejor y mucho más fiable que cualquiera del bullpen de los Rangers. Lo más inteligente, en mi opinión, es no preocuparse por todo el partido y centrarse solo en el momento en el que podamos dar por hecho que Gray estará en el montículo. Apuesto por los Red Sox hasta la quinta entrada.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Red Sox Hit With More Bad Injury News Before MLB Playoffs
item.dc:creator: Keith Watkins
item.description: The Boston Red Sox recalled Anthony Seigler less than a week ago to help fill the roster gap left by Eli White's foot injury. The switch-hitting infielder had contributed during a stretch that lifted Boston into playoff contention. That fill-in role has already been cut short. Seigler went on the injured list September 13 with a right wrist issue, and the latest update paints a discouraging picture for his availability going forward. The Red Sox are 82-70 with 10 games left in the regular season
item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox recalled Anthony Seigler less than a week ago to help fill the roster gap left by Eli White's foot injury. The switch-hitting infielder had contributed during a stretch that lifted Boston into playoff contention.
That fill-in role has already been cut short. Seigler went on the injured list September 13 with a right wrist issue, and the latest update paints a discouraging picture for his availability going forward.
The Red Sox are 82-70 with 10 games left in the regular season. The playoff spot is within reach. The roster is getting thinner.
Infielder Shut Down From Baseball Activities
Seigler has been shut down from all baseball activities for at least a week, according to MassLive's Chris Cotillo.
The wrist flared up again during a plate appearance on Sunday, and he now appears doubtful to return during the regular season.
The timeline makes the math difficult. A minimum of seven days without baseball activities leaves almost no runway to ramp back up before the final game of the season. Even an optimistic recovery would push his return deep into October, if it comes at all.
What Seigler Brought to Boston
Seigler arrived from the Milwaukee Brewers in February alongside Caleb Durbin and Andruw Monasterio. After joining the big league roster in late June, he became part of a stretch that saw Boston win at a historic pace.
He delivered a 4-for-5 performance against the Blue Jays in July that included a leadoff homer and two doubles. In August, he lined a ninth-inning triple that gave Boston the lead against the Marlins when the team needed it most.
Across 171 plate appearances this season, Seigler slashed .250/.331/.405 with three home runs and 13 RBIs. His positional versatility and switch-hitting made him a valuable bench piece for a team building toward October.
Final Word for the Red Sox
Anthony Seigler was brought back to help. Less than a week later, the Red Sox are dealing with another absence.
The wrist issue is the latest in a string of roster hits Boston has absorbed down the stretch. White is done for the regular season. Ceddanne Rafaela remains out until next week. The depth that carried this team through the summer is being tested heading into the final 10 games.
Seigler did enough during his time on the field to earn the recall. Whether he gets another chance this year depends on how far the Red Sox go in October.
